title.zh: 卷九十五 列傳第四十五: 睿宗諸子
title.raw: 卷九十五 列傳第四十五: 睿宗諸子 Volume 95 Biographies 45: Ruizong's Sons

meta.sourceNote: Body replaced from Wikisource raw text after ChineseNotes scrape due to glyph/encoding artifacts.

sentences.zh: 崔日用，滑州靈昌人，其先自博陵徙家焉。

translations.literal: Cui Riyong was a native of Lingchang in Huazhou; his ancestors had moved their family there from Boling.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Riyong was from Lingchang in Huazhou; his forebears had relocated their household from Boling.

sentences.zh: 進士舉，初為芮城尉。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and at first served as magistrate of Ruicheng.
translations.idiomatic: After earning his jinshi degree, he began his career as magistrate of Ruicheng.

sentences.zh: 大足元年，則天幸長安，路次陜州。

translations.literal: In the first year of Dazu, Empress Wu visited Chang'an, passing through Shaan Prefecture on the way.
translations.idiomatic: In 701, when Empress Wu traveled to Chang'an, her route took her through Shaan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 宗楚客時為刺史，日用支供頓事，廣求珍味，稱楚客之命，遍饋從官。

translations.literal: Zong Chuke was then prefect; Riyong managed supplies for the imperial halt, widely sought delicacies, and in Chuke's name distributed them to all accompanying officials.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Chuke was serving as prefect at the time. Riyong handled provisioning for the imperial stopover, procured delicacies far and wide, and distributed them to every member of the entourage in Chuke's name.

sentences.zh: 楚客知而大加賞嘆，盛稱薦之，由是擢為新豐尉。

translations.literal: When Chuke learned of this he was greatly impressed and praised him highly, recommending him strongly; on this basis Riyong was promoted to magistrate of Xinfeng.
translations.idiomatic: Chuke was so pleased when he heard of it that he lavished praise on Riyong and recommended him at length, and Riyong was accordingly promoted to magistrate of Xinfeng.

sentences.zh: 無幾，拜監察御史。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he received appointment as investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 神龍中，秘書監鄭普思納女後宮，潛謀左道，日用遽奏劾之。

translations.literal: During the Shenlong era, Director of the Secretariat Zheng Pusi sent a daughter into the inner palace and secretly plotted heterodox practices; Riyong promptly memorialized impeaching him.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shenlong period (705–707), Zheng Pusi, Director of the Secretariat, placed a daughter in the inner palace and secretly engaged in forbidden cult practices. Riyong immediately submitted an impeachment memorial against him.

sentences.zh: 普思方承恩，中宗不之省。

translations.literal: Pusi was then enjoying imperial favor, and Zhongzong paid no heed.
translations.idiomatic: Pusi was riding high on imperial favor at the time, and Emperor Zhongzong took no notice.

sentences.zh: 日用廷爭懇至，詞甚抗直，普思竟伏其罪。

translations.literal: Riyong argued earnestly at court, his language very forthright; Pusi in the end acknowledged guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Riyong pressed his case passionately in open court debate, speaking with blunt forthrightness, and Pusi ultimately confessed his crimes.

sentences.zh: 時宗楚客、武三思、武延秀等遞為朋黨，日用潛皆附之，驟遷兵部侍郎兼修文館學士。

translations.literal: At that time Zong Chuke, Wu Sansi, Wu Yanxiu, and others formed factions in succession; Riyong secretly attached himself to them all and was abruptly promoted to Vice Minister of War and Academician of the Xiuxian Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Chuke, Wu Sansi, Wu Yanxiu, and their allies were then taking turns as court factions. Riyong quietly attached himself to each in turn and was rapidly promoted to Vice Minister of War and concurrently a Xiuxian Hall academician.

sentences.zh: 中宗暴崩，韋庶人稱制，日用恐禍及己。

translations.literal: When Zhongzong died suddenly, Empress Wei assumed regency, and Riyong feared disaster would reach him.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Zhongzong died suddenly and Empress Wei seized power as regent, Riyong feared he would be caught up in the coming purge.

sentences.zh: 知玄宗將圖義舉，乃因沙門普潤、道士王曄密詣籓邸，深自結納，潛謀翼戴。

translations.literal: Knowing that Xuanzong was planning a righteous rising, he went through the monk Purun and the Daoist Wang Ye to visit the princely residence in secret, binding himself closely and plotting in secret to support and elevate him.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Prince Lin (the future Xuanzong) was planning a coup, he used the monk Purun and the Daoist Wang Ye as intermediaries to visit the prince's residence in secret, pledged himself deeply, and plotted to help place him on the throne.

sentences.zh: 玄宗嘗謂曰：「今謀此舉，直為親，不為身。」

translations.literal: Xuanzong once said to him: "In plotting this undertaking now, it is purely for kin, not for oneself.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong once told him, "In what we are planning now, I act solely for my family—not for my own gain."

sentences.zh: 日用曰：「此乃孝感動天，事必克捷。

translations.literal: Riyong said: "This is filial devotion moving Heaven; the affair is sure to succeed swiftly.
translations.idiomatic: Riyong replied, "Such filial devotion moves Heaven itself—the enterprise is bound to succeed.

sentences.zh: 望速發，出其不意，若少遲延，或恐生變。」

translations.literal: I hope you will launch quickly, catching them unawares; if there is the slightest delay, I fear changes may arise."
translations.idiomatic: Strike at once, while they are unprepared. Even a brief delay may bring unforeseen trouble."

sentences.zh: 及討平韋氏，其夜，令權知雍州長史事。

translations.literal: When the Wei clan was suppressed, that same night he was ordered to act as provisional Administrator of Yong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The night the Wei faction was overthrown, he was appointed acting Administrator of Yong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 以功授銀青光祿大夫、黃門侍郎，參知機務，封齊國公，食實封二百戶。

translations.literal: For his merit he was granted Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Vice Director of the Yellow Gate, participation in state affairs, enfeoffment as Duke of Qi, with an actual fief of two hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was made Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Vice Director of the Yellow Gate, with a seat in deliberating state affairs; he was enfeoffed as Duke of Qi with a substantive fief of two hundred households.

sentences.zh: 為相月餘，與中書侍郎薛稷不協，於中書忿競，由是轉雍州長史，停知政事。

translations.literal: After more than a month as chief minister, he fell out with Vice Director of the Secretariat Xue Ji; they quarreled angrily at the Secretariat, and on this account he was transferred to Administrator of Yong Prefecture and ceased participating in government.
translations.idiomatic: After barely a month as chief minister he clashed with Vice Director Xue Ji; their bitter dispute at the Secretariat cost him his post, and he was reassigned as Administrator of Yong Prefecture with his seat in government withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 尋出為揚州長史，歷婺、汴二州刺史、兗州都督、荊州長史。

translations.literal: Soon he went out as Senior Administrator of Yang Prefecture, and successively served as prefect of Wu and Bian, Military Commissioner of Yan, and Senior Administrator of Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon sent out as Senior Administrator of Yangzhou, then served in turn as prefect of Wu and Bian, Military Commissioner of Yanzhou, and Senior Administrator of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 因入奏事，言：「太平公主謀逆有期，陛下往在宮府，欲有討捕，猶是子道臣道，須用謀用力。

translations.literal: On entering to report affairs he said: "Princess Taiping's plot to rebel has a set time. When Your Majesty was still in the princely residence and wished to suppress it, that was still the way of son and subject—you had to use stratagem and force.
translations.idiomatic: On a visit to court he said, "Princess Taiping's rebellion is imminent. When Your Majesty was still in the princely residence and wished to move against her, you were bound by the roles of son and subject and had to rely on stratagem and force.

sentences.zh: 今既光臨大寶，但須下一制，誰敢不從？

translations.literal: Now that you have ascended the Great Treasure, you need only issue one edict—who would dare not obey?
translations.idiomatic: Now that you occupy the throne, a single edict is all that is required. Who would dare disobey?

sentences.zh: 忽奸宄得志，則禍亂不小。」

translations.literal: If traitors suddenly gain their aim, the calamity and disorder will not be small.
translations.idiomatic: If the traitors gain the upper hand even briefly, the resulting turmoil will be grave indeed."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「誠如此，直恐驚動太上皇，卿宜更思之。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "If it is truly so, I fear only alarming the Retired Emperor; you should think again."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor replied, "If matters stand as you say, I am chiefly afraid of alarming the Retired Emperor. You should reconsider."

sentences.zh: 日用曰：「臣聞天子孝與庶人孝全別。

translations.literal: Riyong said: "I have heard that the filial piety of the Son of Heaven and the filial piety of the common people are wholly different.
translations.idiomatic: Riyong said, "I have heard that the Son of Heaven's filial piety and the commoner's filial piety are entirely different things.

sentences.zh: 庶人孝，謹身節用，承順顏色；

translations.literal: The commoner's filial piety is to keep the body disciplined, economize expenditure, and comply with the parent's countenance;
translations.idiomatic: For the commoner, filial piety means disciplining oneself, living frugally, and deferring to a parent's wishes;

sentences.zh: 天子孝，安國家，定社稷。

translations.literal: the Son of Heaven's filial piety is to secure the state and settle the altars of soil and grain.
translations.idiomatic: for the Son of Heaven it means securing the realm and stabilizing the altars of state.

sentences.zh: 今若逆黨竊發，即大業都棄，豈得成天子之孝乎！

translations.literal: If the rebel faction steals a start now, the great enterprise will all be abandoned—how could that fulfill the Son of Heaven's filial piety!
translations.idiomatic: If the rebels strike now, the imperial enterprise itself will be lost—how could that fulfill a Son of Heaven's filial duty!

sentences.zh: 伏請先定北軍，次收逆黨，即不驚動太上皇。」

translations.literal: I humbly beg that you first secure the Northern Army, then seize the rebel faction—that way the Retired Emperor will not be disturbed."
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to secure the Northern Army first and then arrest the rebels; the Retired Emperor need not be disturbed at all."

sentences.zh: 玄宗從其議。

translations.literal: Xuanzong followed his proposal.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong adopted his plan.

sentences.zh: 及討蕭至忠、竇懷貞之際，又令權檢校雍州長史，加實封通前滿四百戶。

translations.literal: When suppressing Xiao Zhizhong and Dou Huaizhen, he was again ordered to act as provisional Inspector of Yong Prefecture, and his actual fief was increased to four hundred households including previous grants.
translations.idiomatic: During the campaign against Xiao Zhizhong and Dou Huaizhen he was again made provisional Inspector of Yong Prefecture, and his substantive fief was raised to four hundred households in all.

sentences.zh: 尋拜吏部尚書。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 日用嘗采《毛詩》、《大雅》、《小雅》二十篇及司馬相如《封禪書》，因上生日表上之，以申規諷，並述告成之事。

translations.literal: Riyong once selected twenty pieces from the Mao Odes, the Greater and Lesser Elegantiae, and Sima Xiangru's "Letter on the Feng and Shan Sacrifices," and on the occasion of the Emperor's birthday submitted them in a memorial to offer admonition and allusion, also recounting matters of announcing completion.
translations.idiomatic: Riyong once compiled twenty pieces from the Mao Odes, the Greater and Lesser Elegantiae, and Sima Xiangru's Letter on the Feng and Shan Sacrifices, and presented them in a birthday memorial as gentle admonition, together with an account of announcing the completion of great undertakings.

sentences.zh: 手詔答曰：「夫詩者，動天地，感鬼神，厚於人，美於教矣。

translations.literal: An imperial rescript in the Emperor's own hand replied: "Poetry moves Heaven and Earth, touches spirits and ghosts, enriches humanity, and beautifies instruction.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor answered in his own hand: "Poetry moves Heaven and Earth, stirs spirits and ghosts, enriches humankind, and adorns moral instruction.

sentences.zh: 朕志之所尚，思與之齊，庶乎采詩之官，補朕之闕。

translations.literal: What my will esteems, I wish to align with it, hoping that the officers who gather poems may supply my omissions.
translations.idiomatic: What my heart esteems in poetry I wish to match; may the officers who gather songs help remedy my shortcomings.

sentences.zh: 且古者封禪，升中告成，朕以菲德，未明於至道。

translations.literal: Moreover, in antiquity the feng and shan sacrifices ascended Mount Tai and announced completion; I, with meager virtue, am not clear on the utmost Way.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity the feng and shan rites ascended Mount Tai to announce the completion of great deeds; my own virtue is slight, and I am far from grasping the highest Way.

sentences.zh: 竦然以聽，頗壯相如之詞；

translations.literal: Startled, I listened—Xiangru's words quite stirred me;
translations.idiomatic: I listened with awe, and Xiangru's rhetoric indeed stirred me;

sentences.zh: 惕然載懷，復慚夷吾之語。

translations.literal: wary, I bore it in mind, yet again felt shame at Guan Yiwu's words.
translations.idiomatic: yet I bore Guan Zhong's warning in mind as well and felt shame anew.

sentences.zh: 卿洽聞殫見，溫故知新，逮此發揮，益彰忠懇。

translations.literal: You are broadly informed and exhaustively perceptive, warming the old to know the new; in reaching this expression, your loyal earnestness is all the more revealed.
translations.idiomatic: Your learning is broad and your insight complete; in reviving the old to illuminate the new, this presentation shows your loyal earnestness all the more clearly.

sentences.zh: 豈非討蓬山之籍，心不忘於起予；

translations.literal: Is it not that in searching the registers of Mount Penglai, your heart did not forget to rouse me;
translations.idiomatic: Surely in searching the libraries of Penglai you did not forget to awaken me;

sentences.zh: 因蘭殿之祥，言固深於啟沃，朕循環覽諷，用慰於懷。

translations.literal: and on the auspicious day of the Orchid Hall, your words surely went deep in nourishing counsel—I have gone through them repeatedly in recitation, taking comfort in my breast.
translations.idiomatic: and on this auspicious day in the Orchid Hall your words offered counsel of real depth. I have read them again and again, and they comfort my heart.

sentences.zh: 今賜卿衣裳一副、物五十段，以示無言不酬之信也。」

translations.literal: Now I bestow on you one set of robes and fifty lengths of goods, to show the faith that no word goes unrewarded."
translations.idiomatic: I now grant you one set of robes and fifty lengths of goods, as proof that no loyal word goes unrewarded."

sentences.zh: 尋出為常州刺史，削實封三百戶，轉汝州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he went out as prefect of Chang Prefecture; three hundred households were cut from his actual fief, and he was transferred to prefect of Ru Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon sent out as prefect of Changzhou; three hundred households were stripped from his substantive fief, and he was transferred to prefect of Ruzhou.

sentences.zh: 開元七年，差降口賦，特下敕曰：「唐元之際，逆黨構凶，崔日用當時潛論其事，及於戡翦，實預元謀，而所食之封，後以例減。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Kaiyuan, when household levies were reduced by decree, a special edict stated: "At the time of Tang's restoration, the rebel faction plotted violence; Cui Riyong then secretly discussed the matter, and when it came to suppression he truly took part in the original plot—yet the fief he received was later reduced by precedent.
translations.idiomatic: In 719, when household levies were reduced across the empire, a special edict declared: "At the restoration of the Tang, the rebel faction plotted treason. Cui Riyong had secretly discussed the matter beforehand and truly shared in the original design; yet his fief was later reduced under the general rule.

sentences.zh: 功既居多，特宜準初食之封，與二百戶。」

translations.literal: His merit being especially great, it is fitting that his fief match the initial grant of two hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: His merit was outstanding, and his fief should be restored to the original grant of two hundred households."

sentences.zh: 十年，轉并州大都督長史。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was transferred to Senior Administrator of the Metropolitan Area Command at Bing.
translations.idiomatic: In 722 he was transferred to Senior Administrator of the Bingzhou Metropolitan Command.

sentences.zh: 尋卒，時年五十，贈吏部尚書，謚曰昭。

translations.literal: Before long he died, aged fifty; he was posthumously made Minister of Personnel, with the posthumous title Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon afterward at the age of fifty. He was posthumously appointed Minister of Personnel and given the posthumous title Zhao ("Illustrious").

sentences.zh: 後又贈荊州大都督，子宗之襲。

translations.literal: Later he was also posthumously made Metropolitan Governor of Jing; his son Zongzhi inherited.
translations.idiomatic: He was later posthumously made Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhou as well; his son Zongzhi inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 日用才辯過人，見事敏速，每朝廷有事，轉禍為福，以取富貴。

translations.literal: Riyong's talent and eloquence surpassed others; he saw affairs with quick perception, and whenever the court had trouble he turned calamity into blessing to gain wealth and rank.
translations.idiomatic: Riyong's eloquence and quick wit surpassed others'. Whenever crisis struck the court he turned disaster to advantage and secured wealth and high office.

sentences.zh: 及先天已後，復求入相，竟亦不遂。

translations.literal: After the Xiantian era he again sought to enter the chancellorship, but in the end did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: After the Xiantian period (712–713) he sought a return to the chancellorship but never achieved it.

sentences.zh: 常謂人曰：「吾一生行事，皆臨時制變，不必重專守始謀。

translations.literal: He often told people: "In all my life's actions I have adapted on the spot; one need not cling heavily to the original plan.
translations.idiomatic: He often said, "Everything I have done in life I decided on the spot; there is no need to cling stubbornly to one's first plan.

sentences.zh: 每一念之，不覺芒刺在於背也。」

translations.literal: Each time I think of it, I cannot help feeling bristles like awls in my back.
translations.idiomatic: Even now, whenever I think of it, I feel as though needles were pricking my back."

sentences.zh: 崔日知日用從父兄日知，亦有吏幹。

translations.literal: Cui Rizhi—Riyong's paternal cousin Rizhi—also had administrative ability.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Rizhi, Riyong's paternal cousin, likewise possessed administrative talent.

sentences.zh: 景雲中為洛州司馬。

translations.literal: During Jingyun he was Vice Prefect of Luo.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jingyun era (710–711) he served as Vice Prefect of Luozhou.

sentences.zh: 會譙王重福入東都作亂，群臣皆避難逃匿，日知獨督率人吏赴留守，與屯營合勢討賊。

translations.literal: When Prince of Qiao Chongfu entered the Eastern Capital to rebel, the ministers all fled and hid; Rizhi alone led officials and clerks to the garrison command, joining camp forces to suppress the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Chongfu of Qiao raised rebellion in the Eastern Capital, the officials all fled and hid; Rizhi alone rallied the local staff to the garrison command and joined the encamped troops to suppress the rebels.

sentences.zh: 重福既死，以功加銀青光祿大夫，累遷京兆尹。

translations.literal: After Chongfu died, for his merit he was promoted to Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and rose in succession to Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: After Chongfu's death Rizhi was promoted to Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Splendid Happiness for his service and eventually rose to Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 坐贓為御史李如璧所劾，左遷歙縣丞，俄又歷遷殿中監。

translations.literal: For corruption he was impeached by Censor Li Rubi, demoted to Assistant Magistrate of She, and before long was promoted in succession to Director of the Palace Domestic Service.
translations.idiomatic: Impeached for corruption by Censor Li Rubi, he was demoted to assistant magistrate of She County but was soon promoted again, eventually reaching Director of the Palace Domestic Service.

sentences.zh: 日知素與張說友善，說薦之，奏請授御史大夫，上不許。

translations.literal: Rizhi had long been friendly with Zhang Yue; Yue recommended him and memorialized requesting appointment as Censor-in-Chief, but the Emperor did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: Rizhi had long been on good terms with Zhang Yue, who recommended him and petitioned for his appointment as Censor-in-Chief; the Emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 遂以為左羽林懷大將軍，而以河南尹崔隱甫為御史大夫，隱甫由是與說不葉。

translations.literal: He was therefore made General of the Left Feathered Forest Guard, while Metropolitan Governor of Henan Cui Yinpu was made Censor-in-Chief; Yinpu on this account was at odds with Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Rizhi was instead made General of the Left Feathered Forest Guard, while Cui Yinpu, Metropolitan Governor of Henan, was appointed Censor-in-Chief; Yinpu and Yue became estranged as a result.

sentences.zh: 日知俄遷太常卿。

translations.literal: Rizhi was soon transferred to Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Rizhi was soon transferred to Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 自以歷任年久，每朝士參集，常與尚書同列，時人號為「尚書裏行」，遂為口實。

translations.literal: Considering that he had served many years, whenever courtiers assembled he was regularly ranked with the Ministers; people of the time called him "Minister in practice," and it became a byword.
translations.idiomatic: Because he had served so long, whenever officials gathered at court he was placed in the same row as the Ministers; contemporaries dubbed him "the Minister in practice," and the nickname stuck.

sentences.zh: 開元十六年，出為潞州大都督府長史。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Kaiyuan he went out as Senior Administrator of the Metropolitan Area Command at Lu.
translations.idiomatic: In 728 he was sent out as Senior Administrator of the Luzhou Metropolitan Command.

sentences.zh: 尋以年老致仕，卒，謚曰襄。

translations.literal: Before long, on account of age he retired; he died, with the posthumous title Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: He soon retired on grounds of age and later died; he was given the posthumous title Xiang ("Assisting").

sentences.zh: 張嘉貞，蒲州猗氏人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Jiazhen was a native of Yishi in Pu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jiazhen was a native of Yishi in Pu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 弱冠應五經舉，拜平鄉尉，坐事免歸鄉里。

translations.literal: At twenty he entered the Five Classics examination, was appointed magistrate of Pingxiang, and for an offense was dismissed and returned to his home district.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty he took the Five Classics examination, was appointed magistrate of Pingxiang, but was dismissed for an offense and returned home.

sentences.zh: 長安中，侍御史張循憲為河東采訪使，薦嘉貞材堪憲官，請以己之官秩授之。

translations.literal: During the Chang'an era, Attending Censor Zhang Xunxian was Investigation Commissioner of Hedong; he recommended Jiazhen's talent as fit for a censor's post and asked to transfer his own rank to him.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chang'an period (701–705), Attending Censor Zhang Xunxian, serving as Investigation Commissioner of Hedong, recommended Jiazhen as qualified for a censor's post and offered to surrender his own rank to secure the appointment.

sentences.zh: 則天召見，垂簾與之言，嘉貞奏曰：「以臣草萊而得入謁九重，是千載一遇也。

translations.literal: Empress Wu summoned him for audience, spoke with him behind the screen, and Jiazhen memorialized: "That I, a man of the wilds, should gain audience in the Ninefold Enclosure is a meeting once in a thousand years.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu summoned him for audience and spoke with him from behind the screen. Jiazhen said, "That a commoner like myself should gain audience in the inner palace is a chance that comes once in a thousand years.

sentences.zh: 咫尺之間，如隔雲務，竟不睹日月，恐君臣之道有所未盡。」

translations.literal: Within a foot's distance it is as if separated by clouds and mist—I cannot finally see sun and moon; I fear the way of ruler and minister is not fully realized.
translations.idiomatic: Yet within a foot's distance I am separated as if by clouds and mist and cannot behold Your Majesty's face; I fear the bond between ruler and subject is not fully honored."

sentences.zh: 則天遽令卷簾，與語大悅，擢拜監察御史。

translations.literal: Empress Wu immediately ordered the screen raised; she spoke with him with great delight and promoted him to investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu immediately ordered the screen raised, spoke with him at length with great pleasure, and promoted him to investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 累遷中書舍人，歷秦州都督、并州長史，為政嚴肅，甚為人吏所畏。

translations.literal: He rose in succession to Secretariat Drafter, and served as Military Commissioner of Qin and Senior Administrator of Bing; his governance was stern and severe, and officials and clerks greatly feared him.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Secretariat Drafter and served in turn as Military Commissioner of Qinzhou and Senior Administrator of Bingzhou; his administration was stern and severe, and officials and clerks alike feared him.

sentences.zh: 開元初，因奏事至京師，上聞其善政，數加賞慰。

translations.literal: Early in Kaiyuan, on reporting affairs he came to the capital; the Emperor heard of his good governance and repeatedly praised and comforted him.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kaiyuan reign he came to the capital on official business; the Emperor heard reports of his excellent administration and repeatedly praised and encouraged him.

sentences.zh: 嘉貞因奏曰：「臣少孤，兄弟相依以至今。

translations.literal: Jiazhen thereupon memorialized: "I was orphaned young; my brothers have relied on one another until today.
translations.idiomatic: Jiazhen then said, "I lost my parents young; my brothers have depended on one another ever since.

sentences.zh: 臣弟嘉祐，今授鄯州別駕，與臣各在一方，同心離居，魂絕萬里。

translations.literal: My younger brother Jiayou is now appointed Vice Prefect of Bin; he and I are each in a different region—of one heart yet dwelling apart, our spirits severed by ten thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: My younger brother Jiayou has just been appointed Vice Prefect of Binzhou; we are posted to opposite ends of the empire, united in heart yet separated in body, our spirits torn apart by ten thousand li.

sentences.zh: 乞移就臣側近，臣兄弟盡力報國，死無所恨。」

translations.literal: I beg that he be transferred near me; my brother and I will exhaust our strength in serving the state and die without regret.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that he be transferred to a post near mine; my brother and I will serve the state with all our strength and die without regret."

sentences.zh: 上嘉其友愛，特改嘉祐為忻州刺史。

translations.literal: The Emperor commended his brotherly affection and specially changed Jiayou to prefect of Xin.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor admired his brotherly devotion and specially transferred Jiayou to prefect of Xinzhou.

sentences.zh: 時突厥九姓新來內附，散居太原以北，嘉貞奏請置軍以鎮之，於是始於并州置天兵軍，以嘉貞為使。

translations.literal: At that time the nine surnames of the Turks had newly submitted and were scattered north of Taiyuan; Jiazhen memorialized requesting establishment of an army to garrison them, and on this basis the Heavenly Troops Army was first established at Bing, with Jiazhen as commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The nine Turkic clans had recently submitted and were scattered north of Taiyuan. Jiazhen petitioned to establish a garrison army, and the Heavenly Troops Army was accordingly founded at Bingzhou with Jiazhen as its commissioner.

sentences.zh: 六年春，嘉貞又入朝。

translations.literal: In the spring of the sixth year Jiazhen again entered court.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the sixth year (718) Jiazhen returned to court.

sentences.zh: 俄有告其在軍奢僭及贓賄者，御史大夫王晙因而劾奏之，按驗無狀，上將加告者反坐之罪。

translations.literal: Before long someone reported that in the army he had been extravagant and presumptuous and had taken bribes; Censor-in-Chief Wang Jun thereupon impeached him; investigation found no basis, and the Emperor was about to impose counter-charges on the accuser.
translations.idiomatic: Soon someone accused him of extravagance and corruption in the army. Censor-in-Chief Wang Jun impeached him on that basis, but the investigation found no evidence, and the Emperor was about to punish the accuser for false reporting.

sentences.zh: 嘉貞奏曰：「昔者天子聽政於上，瞍賦矇誦，百工諫，庶人謗，而後天子斟酌焉。

translations.literal: Jiazhen memorialized: "In antiquity the Son of Heaven heard government above; the blind sang and the sightless recited, the hundred craftsmen remonstrated, and the common people slandered—only then did the Son of Heaven weigh these matters.
translations.idiomatic: Jiazhen said, "In antiquity the Son of Heaven heard government from above: the blind sang ballads, the sightless recited, craftsmen remonstrated, and commoners criticized—only then did the ruler weigh all these voices.

sentences.zh: 今反坐此輩，是塞言者之路，則天下之事無由上達。

translations.literal: If we now impose counter-charges on these men, we block the road of those who speak—then affairs under Heaven have no way to reach above.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty punishes these accusers now, you will block the path of those who speak, and nothing under Heaven will reach Your Majesty's ears.

sentences.zh: 特望免此罪，以廣謗誦之道。」

translations.literal: I specially hope to exempt them from this punishment, to broaden the way of criticism and recitation.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to waive punishment in this case and keep the channels of criticism open."

sentences.zh: 從之，遂令減死，自是帝以嘉貞為忠。

translations.literal: The Emperor followed this; he then ordered reduction of the death penalty, and from this the Emperor regarded Jiazhen as loyal.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor agreed and commuted the death sentence; from that time he regarded Jiazhen as a loyal minister.

sentences.zh: 嘉貞又嘗奏曰：「今誌力方壯，是效命之秋，更三數年，即衰老無能為也。

translations.literal: Jiazhen also once memorialized: "Now my will and strength are in their prime—this is the season to devote my life; in another few years I will be old and feeble and able to do nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Jiazhen also once said, "My mind and strength are at their peak—this is the season to serve with my life. In a few more years I will be old and useless.

sentences.zh: 惟陛下早垂任使，死且不憚。」

translations.literal: I only hope Your Majesty will early bestow employment on me—I will not fear even death.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to employ me while I am still able; I do not fear death."

sentences.zh: 上以其明辯，尤重之。

translations.literal: The Emperor, because of his clear eloquence, especially valued him.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor valued him all the more for his clarity and eloquence.

sentences.zh: 八年春，宋璟、蘇颋罷知政事，擢嘉貞為中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: In the spring of the eighth year Song Jing and Su Ting ceased participating in government; Jiazhen was promoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat and Associate Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of 720, when Song Jing and Su Ting left office, Jiazhen was promoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat and appointed Associate Chief Minister.

sentences.zh: 數月，加銀青光祿大夫，遷中書令。

translations.literal: Within months he was given Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and transferred to Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Within months he was made Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and promoted to Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 嘉貞斷決敏速，善於敷奏，然性強躁自用，頗為時論所譏。

translations.literal: Jiazhen decided cases with quick perception and was skilled at presenting memorials, yet his nature was forceful, impatient, and self-willed, and he was considerably ridiculed in contemporary opinion.
translations.idiomatic: Jiazhen decided cases with swift judgment and was skilled at court presentation, but his nature was forceful, impatient, and self-willed, and contemporary opinion often criticized him.

sentences.zh: 時中書舍人苗延嗣、呂太一、考功員外郎員嘉靜、殿中侍御史崔訓，皆嘉貞所引，位列清要，常在嘉貞門下共議朝政，時人為之語曰：「令公四俊，苗、呂、崔、員。」

translations.literal: At that time Secretariat Drafters Miao Yansi and Lü Taiyi, Director of Evaluations Yuan Jiajing, and Palace Attending Censor Cui Xun were all introduced by Jiazhen, held posts of clear importance, and were constantly at Jiazhen's gate jointly discussing court government; people of the time made a saying of it: "The Chief Minister's four talents: Miao, Lü, Cui, and Yuan."
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat Drafters Miao Yansi and Lü Taiyi, Director of Evaluations Yuan Jiajing, and Palace Attending Censor Cui Xun were all Jiazhen's protégés, holding prestigious posts and constantly gathered at his door to discuss policy. A contemporary saying ran: "The Chief Minister's four talents: Miao, Lü, Cui, and Yuan."

sentences.zh: 開元十年，車駕幸東都。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Kaiyuan the imperial carriage visited the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In 722 the Emperor traveled to the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 有洛陽主簿王鈞為嘉貞修宅，將以求御史，因受贓事發，上特令朝堂集眾決殺之。

translations.literal: The Luoyang Registrar Wang Jun built a residence for Jiazhen, intending thereby to seek the post of censor; because a bribery affair came to light, the Emperor specially ordered assembly at court to decide and execute him.
translations.idiomatic: The Luoyang Registrar Wang Jun had built a residence for Jiazhen in hopes of securing a censor's post; when a bribery case came to light, the Emperor ordered a public assembly at court to decide his execution.

sentences.zh: 嘉貞促所由速其刑以滅口，乃歸罪於御史大夫韋抗、中丞韋虛心，皆貶黜之。

translations.literal: Jiazhen urged the responsible officials to hasten his punishment to silence him, then shifted blame onto Censor-in-Chief Wei Kang and Vice Censor-in-Chief Wei Xuxin, and both were demoted.
translations.idiomatic: Jiazhen pressed the officials to hurry the execution and silence him, then shifted blame onto Censor-in-Chief Wei Kang and Vice Censor-in-Chief Wei Xuxin; both were demoted.

sentences.zh: 其冬，秘書監姜皎犯罪，嘉貞又附會王守一奏請杖之，皎遂死於路。

translations.literal: That winter Director of the Secretariat Jiang Jiao committed an offense; Jiazhen again joined Wang Shouyi in memorializing to request beating with the staff, and Jiao died on the road.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Director of the Secretariat Jiang Jiao was convicted of a crime; Jiazhen again joined Wang Shouyi in petitioning for corporal punishment, and Jiang died on the road into exile.

sentences.zh: 俄而廣州都督裴伷先下獄，上召侍臣問當何罪，嘉貞又請杖之。

translations.literal: Before long Military Commissioner of Guangzhou Pei Xianxian was imprisoned; the Emperor summoned attending ministers to ask what punishment was fitting, and Jiazhen again requested beating with the staff.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Military Commissioner of Guangzhou Pei Xianxian was imprisoned; the Emperor asked his ministers what sentence was appropriate, and Jiazhen again petitioned for corporal punishment.

sentences.zh: 兵部尚書張說進曰：「臣聞刑不上大夫，以其近於君也。

translations.literal: Minister of War Zhang Yue advanced and said: "I have heard that punishment does not reach the grand masters, because they are close to the ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of War Zhang Yue stepped forward and said, "I have heard that punishment does not reach high officials, because they stand close to the ruler.

sentences.zh: 故曰：『士可殺，不可辱。』

translations.literal: Therefore it is said: 'A gentleman may be killed but not humiliated.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the saying: 'A gentleman may be killed, but he must not be humiliated.'

sentences.zh: 臣今秋受詔巡邊，中途聞姜皎以罪於朝堂決杖，配流而死。

translations.literal: This autumn I received orders to tour the frontier; midway I heard that Jiang Jiao, for his crime, was beaten with the staff at court and died on assignment to exile.
translations.idiomatic: This autumn I received orders to tour the frontier; midway I learned that Jiang Jiao had been beaten at court for his crime and died on the road into exile.

sentences.zh: 皎官是三品，亦有微功。

translations.literal: Jiao's office was third rank, and he also had slight merit.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang held third-rank office and had rendered some service.

sentences.zh: 若其有犯，應死即殺，應流即流，不宜決杖廷辱，以卒伍待之。

translations.literal: If he had an offense, if death was fitting then kill him, if exile was fitting then exile him—he should not have been beaten with the staff and humiliated at court, treated like a common soldier.
translations.idiomatic: If he was guilty, let him be executed if death was warranted or exiled if exile was warranted; he should not have been beaten and humiliated at court as though he were a common soldier.

sentences.zh: 且律有八議，勛貴在焉。

translations.literal: Moreover, the law has the Eight Deliberations, and meritorious nobles are among them.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the law provides the Eight Deliberations, under which meritorious nobles are protected.

sentences.zh: 皎事已往，不可追悔。

translations.literal: Jiao's affair is already past and cannot be regretted.
translations.idiomatic: What is done to Jiang cannot be undone.

sentences.zh: 伷先只宜據狀流貶，不可輕又決罰。」

translations.literal: Xianxian should only be exiled according to the facts of the case; he must not lightly be subjected again to judicial punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Pei should be exiled according to the facts of his case; he must not be beaten again on a whim."

sentences.zh: 上然其言。

translations.literal: The Emperor approved his words.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 嘉貞不悅，退謂說曰：「何言事之深也？」

translations.literal: Jiazhen was displeased; withdrawing he said to Yue: "Why speak so deeply on the matter?
translations.idiomatic: Jiazhen was displeased. As he withdrew he said to Yue, "Why press the point so hard?"

sentences.zh: 說曰：「宰相者，時來即為，豈能長據？

translations.literal: Yue said: "A chief minister comes to office when the time arrives—how can one hold it long?
translations.idiomatic: Yue replied, "A chief minister takes office when the time comes—who can hold the post forever?

sentences.zh: 若貴臣盡當可杖，但恐吾等行當及之。

translations.literal: If all noble ministers may be beaten with the staff, I fear only that we in turn will soon reach that fate.
translations.idiomatic: If every noble minister may be beaten, I fear we ourselves will soon face the same fate.

sentences.zh: 此言非為伷先，乃為天下士君子也。」

translations.literal: These words are not for Xianxian's sake but for gentlemen and scholars under Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: I spoke not for Pei's sake but for gentlemen and scholars everywhere."

sentences.zh: 初，嘉貞為兵部員外郎，時張說為侍郎。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Jiazhen was Vice Director of the Ministry of War, Zhang Yue was Vice Minister.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Jiazhen was Vice Director of the Ministry of War, Zhang Yue was Vice Minister.

sentences.zh: 及是，說位在嘉貞下，既無所推讓，說頗不平，因以此言激怒嘉貞，由是與說不葉。

translations.literal: Now Yue's rank was below Jiazhen's; since there was no yielding on either side, Yue was quite resentful and used these words to provoke Jiazhen; on this account he and Yue were at odds.
translations.idiomatic: Now Yue ranked below Jiazhen, and with no deference on either side Yue was deeply resentful; he used these words deliberately to provoke Jiazhen, and the two became estranged.

sentences.zh: 上又以嘉貞弟嘉祐為金吾將軍，兄弟並居將相之位，甚為時人之所畏憚。

translations.literal: The Emperor also made Jiazhen's younger brother Jiayou General of the Golden Guards; the brothers both held posts of general and minister, and people of the time greatly feared them.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor also appointed Jiazhen's younger brother Jiayou as General of the Golden Guards; with both brothers holding posts of general and minister, contemporaries feared them greatly.

sentences.zh: 十一年，上幸太原行在所，嘉祐贓汙事發。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year the Emperor visited the traveling palace at Taiyuan; Jiayou's corruption came to light.
translations.idiomatic: In 723, when the Emperor visited the traveling palace at Taiyuan, Jiayou's corruption was exposed.

sentences.zh: 張說勸嘉貞素服待罪，不得入謁，因出為幽州刺史，說遂代為中書令。

translations.literal: Zhang Yue urged Jiazhen to wear plain dress and await punishment, forbidding him audience; he was therefore sent out as prefect of You, and Yue then replaced him as Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yue urged Jiazhen to wear mourning dress and await judgment, barring him from court audience; Jiazhen was sent out as prefect of Youzhou, and Yue replaced him as Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 嘉貞惋恨，謂人曰：「中書令幸有二員，何相迫之甚也！」

translations.literal: Jiazhen was aggrieved and told people: "Fortunately there are two Directors of the Secretariat—why press me so hard!
translations.idiomatic: Jiazhen was bitter and said to others, "There are fortunately two Directors of the Secretariat—why hound me so relentlessly!"

sentences.zh: 明年，復拜戶部尚書，兼益州長史，判都督事。

translations.literal: The next year he was again appointed Minister of Revenue and concurrently Senior Administrator of Yi, with authority over the military commissioner's affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was reappointed Minister of Revenue and concurrently Senior Administrator of Yizhou, with authority over the military commissioner's affairs.

sentences.zh: 敕嘉貞就中書省與宰相會宴，嘉貞既恨張說擠己，因攘袂勃罵，源乾曜、王晙共和解之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Jiazhen to attend a banquet with the chief ministers at the Secretariat; Jiazhen, resenting Zhang Yue's squeezing him out, thereupon rolled up his sleeves and burst into furious abuse; Yuan Qianyao and Wang Jun together reconciled them.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ordered Jiazhen to attend a Secretariat banquet with the chief ministers; still resenting Zhang Yue's maneuver against him, Jiazhen rolled up his sleeves and erupted in furious abuse until Yuan Qianyao and Wang Jun intervened to calm him.

sentences.zh: 明年，坐與王守一交往，左轉臺州刺史。

translations.literal: The next year, for associating with Wang Shouyi, he was transferred left to prefect of Tai.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, for associating with Wang Shouyi, he was demoted to prefect of Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 復代盧從願為工部尚書、定州刺史，知北平軍事，累封河東侯。

translations.literal: He again replaced Lu Congyuan as Minister of Works and prefect of Ding, with authority over Beiping military affairs, and was enfeoffed in succession as Marquis of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: He again replaced Lu Congyuan as Minister of Works and prefect of Dingzhou, with authority over Beiping military affairs, and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 將行，上自賦詩，詔百僚於上東門外餞之。

translations.literal: As he was about to depart, the Emperor himself composed a poem and ordered the hundred officials to see him off outside the Upper East Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Before his departure the Emperor composed a poem in his honor and ordered the officials to see him off outside the Upper East Gate.

sentences.zh: 至州，於恆嶽廟中立頌，嘉貞自為其文，乃書於石，其碑用白石為之，素質黑文，甚為奇麗。

translations.literal: On reaching the prefecture he erected a eulogy at the Heng Mountain temple; Jiazhen wrote the text himself and had it carved on stone; the stele was made of white stone with plain substance and black inscription, very striking and beautiful.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching his post he erected a eulogy stele at the Mount Heng temple, composing the text himself and carving it on white stone with black inscription—a work of striking beauty.

sentences.zh: 先是，嶽祠為遠近祈賽，有錢數百萬，嘉貞自以為頌文之功，納其數萬。

translations.literal: Earlier the mountain shrine had been used for prayers and offerings from far and near, with several million in cash; Jiazhen, considering it the merit of his eulogy text, took several tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: The shrine had accumulated several million in cash from offerings near and far; Jiazhen, claiming the merit of his eulogy, took tens of thousands for himself.

sentences.zh: 十七年，嘉貞以疾請就醫東都，制從之。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year Jiazhen, on account of illness, requested to seek medical treatment in the Eastern Capital; an edict granted this.
translations.idiomatic: In 729 Jiazhen, ill, petitioned to seek treatment in the Eastern Capital; the Emperor granted his request.

sentences.zh: 至都，目瞑無所見，上令醫人內直郎田休裕、郎將呂弘泰馳傳往省療之。

translations.literal: On reaching the capital his eyes were closed and he could see nothing; the Emperor ordered physicians Inner Attendant Tian Xiuyu and Commandant Lü Hongtai to hurry by relay post to visit and treat him.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching the capital he had gone blind; the Emperor dispatched the physicians Inner Attendant Tian Xiuyu and Commandant Lü Hongtai by relay post to treat him.

sentences.zh: 其秋卒，年六十四，贈益州大都督。

translations.literal: That autumn he died, aged sixty-four; he was posthumously made Metropolitan Governor of Yi.
translations.idiomatic: He died that autumn at the age of sixty-four and was posthumously appointed Metropolitan Governor of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 謚曰恭肅。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Gongsu.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the posthumous title Gongsu ("Respectful and Solemn").

sentences.zh: 嘉貞雖久歷清要，然不立田園。

translations.literal: Although Jiazhen had long held posts of clear importance, he did not establish estates.
translations.idiomatic: Though Jiazhen had long held prestigious posts, he never established landed estates.

sentences.zh: 及在定州，所親有勸植田業者，嘉貞曰：「吾忝歷官榮，曾任國相，未死之際，豈憂饑餒？

translations.literal: When he was at Ding, intimates urged him to plant estates; Jiazhen said: "I have disgracefully enjoyed the glory of office and once served as state chief minister—before I die, how could I worry about hunger?
translations.idiomatic: At Dingzhou some associates urged him to acquire farmland. Jiazhen said, "I have enjoyed the honors of high office and once served as chief minister—before I die, why should I fear hunger?

sentences.zh: 若負譴責，雖富田莊，亦無用也。

translations.literal: If I bear censure and punishment, even rich estates and manors are of no use.
translations.idiomatic: If I fall under censure and punishment, even vast estates will be useless.

sentences.zh: 比見朝士廣占良田，及身沒後，皆為無賴子弟作酒色之資，甚無謂也。」

translations.literal: I have lately seen court gentlemen widely seize good fields; after their deaths these all become resources for worthless younger kin for wine and women—very pointless.
translations.idiomatic: I have lately seen officials seize vast estates, only to leave them after death as resources for worthless sons and nephews to squander on wine and women—what folly that is."

sentences.zh: 聞者皆嘆伏。

translations.literal: Those who heard all sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: All who heard him sighed in admiration.

sentences.zh: 初，嘉貞作相，薦萬年縣主簿韓朝宗，擢為監察御史。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Jiazhen became chief minister, he recommended Han Chaozong, Registrar of Wannian County, and promoted him to investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiazhen first became chief minister he recommended Han Chaozong, registrar of Wannian County, and promoted him to investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 及嘉貞卒後十數歲，朝宗為京兆尹，因奏曰：「自陛下臨御已來，所用宰相，皆進退以禮，善始令終，身雖已沒，子孫咸在朝廷。

translations.literal: More than ten years after Jiazhen's death, Chaozong as Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao memorialized: "Since Your Majesty ascended the throne, the chief ministers employed have all advanced and retired with propriety, beginning well and ending well; though their persons have passed, their descendants all remain at court.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten years after Jiazhen's death, Chaozong, now Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao, memorialized: "Since Your Majesty's accession, every chief minister appointed has risen and retired with propriety, beginning and ending well; though they have died, their descendants still serve at court.

sentences.zh: 唯張嘉貞晚年一子，今猶未登官序。」

translations.literal: Only Zhang Jiazhen's one son in his later years has still not entered the official roster.
translations.idiomatic: Only Zhang Jiazhen's son, born in his later years, has still not entered official service."

sentences.zh: 上亦惘然，遽令召之，賜名延賞，特拜左內率府兵曹參軍。

translations.literal: The Emperor too was moved; he immediately ordered him summoned, bestowed the name Yanbao, and specially appointed him Military Staff Officer of the Left Inner Rate.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was moved as well and immediately summoned the youth, bestowing the name Yanbao and specially appointing him Military Staff Officer of the Left Inner Rate.

sentences.zh: 德宗朝，位至宰輔，自有傳。

translations.literal: In Dezong's reign he reached the rank of chief minister; he has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Dezong he rose to chief minister; his career is recorded in a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 張嘉祐嘉祐，有幹略，自右金吾將軍貶浦陽府折沖，至二十五年，為相州刺史。

translations.literal: Zhang Jiayou had ability and strategy; from Right General of the Golden Guards he was demoted to Colonel of the Puyang Garrison, and by the twenty-fifth year he was prefect of Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jiayou was capable and resourceful. Demoted from Right General of the Golden Guards to colonel of the Puyang garrison, by 737 he had become prefect of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 相州自開元已來，刺史死貶者十數人，嘉祐訪知尉遲迥周末為相州總管，身死國難，乃立其神祠以邀福。

translations.literal: Since Kaiyuan, more than ten prefects of Xiang had died or been demoted in office; Jiayou learned that Yuwen Jiong at the end of the Northern Zhou had been Area Commander of Xiang and died for the state's calamity, and therefore established his spirit shrine to seek blessing.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Kaiyuan reign more than ten Xiangzhou prefects had died or been demoted in office. Jiayou learned that Yuwen Jiong had served as area commander of Xiang at the end of the Northern Zhou and died for the state, and he established a shrine to Jiong's spirit to seek divine protection.

sentences.zh: 經三考，改左金吾將軍。

translations.literal: After three evaluations he was transferred to Left General of the Golden Guards.
translations.idiomatic: After three evaluations he was transferred to Left General of the Golden Guards.

sentences.zh: 後吳兢為鄴郡守，又加尉遲神冕服。

translations.literal: Later when Wu Jing was prefect of Ye, he again added imperial regalia to Yuwen's spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Wu Jing became prefect of Ye, he added imperial regalia to Yuwen's spirit image as well.

sentences.zh: 自後郡守無患。

translations.literal: From then on prefects had no troubles.
translations.idiomatic: From then on prefects of the commandery suffered no mishaps.

sentences.zh: 蕭嵩，貞觀初左僕射、宋國公瑀之曾侄孫。

translations.literal: Xiao Song was the great-grandnephew of Xiao Yu, Left Vice Director of the Secretariat and Duke of Song in early Zhenguan.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Song was the great-grandnephew of Xiao Yu, Left Vice Director of the Secretariat and Duke of Song in early Zhenguan.

sentences.zh: 祖鈞，中書舍人，有名於時。

translations.literal: His grandfather Jun was a Secretariat Drafter, famous in his time.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Jun had been a Secretariat Drafter renowned in his day.

sentences.zh: 嵩美須髯，儀形偉麗。

translations.literal: Song had a beautiful beard and moustache and a grand, imposing appearance.
translations.idiomatic: Song had a magnificent beard and a grand, imposing bearing.

sentences.zh: 初，娶會稽賀晦女，與吳郡陸象先為僚婿。

translations.literal: At first he married the daughter of He Hui of Kuaiji and with Lu Xiangxian of Wu Commandery became brothers-in-law through their wives.
translations.idiomatic: He first married the daughter of He Hui of Kuaiji and thereby became brothers-in-law with Lu Xiangxian of Wu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 象先時為洛陽尉，宰相子，門望甚高。

translations.literal: Xiangxian was then Vice Magistrate of Luoyang, a chief minister's son, of very high family standing.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangxian was then Vice Magistrate of Luoyang, a chief minister's son of very high family standing.

sentences.zh: 嵩尚未入仕，宣州人夏榮稱有相術，謂象先曰：「陸郎十年內位極人臣，然不及蕭郎一門盡貴，官位高而有壽。」

translations.literal: Song had not yet entered office; Xia Rong of Xuan Prefecture, who claimed skill in physiognomy, told Xiangxian: "Within ten years Master Lu will reach the utmost of human rank, yet he will not equal Master Xiao's whole clan in nobility—high office and long life.
translations.idiomatic: Song had not yet entered office. Xia Rong of Xuanzhou, who claimed skill in physiognomy, told Xiangxian, "Within ten years you will reach the highest rank, yet you will not equal the Xiao clan in nobility—they will hold high office and enjoy long life."

sentences.zh: 時人未之許。

translations.literal: People of the time did not approve this.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries did not believe him.

sentences.zh: 神龍元年，嵩調補洺州參軍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shenlong Song was transferred to fill the post of Administrator of Ming Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In 705 Song was appointed administrator of Mingzhou.

sentences.zh: 尋而侍中、扶陽王桓彥範出為洺州刺史，見之推重，待以殊禮。

translations.literal: Before long Attending Secretariat Director and Prince of Fuyang Huan Yanfan went out as prefect of Ming; on seeing Song he esteemed him and treated him with special courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Attending Secretariat Director Huan Yanfan, Prince of Fuyang, went out as prefect of Mingzhou, esteemed Song on meeting him, and treated him with exceptional courtesy.

sentences.zh: 景雲元年，為醴泉尉。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingyun he was magistrate of Liquan.
translations.idiomatic: In 710 he served as magistrate of Liquan.

sentences.zh: 時陸象先已為中書侍郎，引為監察御史。

translations.literal: At that time Lu Xiangxian was already Vice Director of the Secretariat and brought him in as investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xiangxian was then Vice Director of the Secretariat and secured his appointment as investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 及象先知政事，嵩又驟遷殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: When Xiangxian came to participate in government, Song was again abruptly promoted to Palace Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiangxian entered the government, Song was rapidly promoted to Palace Attending Censor.

sentences.zh: 開元初，為中書舍人。

translations.literal: Early in Kaiyuan he was Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kaiyuan reign he became Secretariat Drafter.

sentences.zh: 與崔琳、王丘、齊澣同列，皆以嵩寡學術，未異之，而紫微令姚崇許其致遠，眷之特深。

translations.literal: He was ranked with Cui Lin, Wang Qiu, and Qi Huan; they all considered Song lacking in learning and did not regard him as unusual, but Director of the Purple Asterism Yao Chong approved his reaching far and favored him especially.
translations.idiomatic: He served alongside Cui Lin, Wang Qiu, and Qi Huan, who all regarded him as poorly educated and unremarkable, but Yao Chong, Director of the Purple Asterism, foresaw his future success and favored him deeply.

sentences.zh: 歷宋州刺史，三遷為尚書左丞、兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: He served as prefect of Song and after three promotions became Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: He served as prefect of Songzhou and after three promotions became Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 十五年，涼州刺史、河西節度王君滷恃眾每歲攻擊吐蕃。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year Wang Junyao, prefect of Liang and Military Commissioner of Hexi, relying on his forces attacked Tibet every year.
translations.idiomatic: In 727 Wang Junyao, prefect of Liangzhou and Military Commissioner of Hexi, relying on his large force attacked Tibet every year.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃大將悉諾邏恭祿及燭龍莽布支攻陷瓜州城，執刺史田元獻及君滷父壽，盡取城中軍資及倉糧，仍毀其城而去。

translations.literal: The Tibetan generals Sinoluogonglu and Zhulongmangbuzhi captured Guazhou city, seized Prefect Tian Yuanxian and Junyao's father Shou, took all military stores and granary grain in the city, and still destroyed the city before departing.
translations.idiomatic: The Tibetan generals Sinoluogonglu and Zhulongmangbuzhi captured Guazhou, seized Prefect Tian Yuanxian and Junyao's father Shou, stripped the city of all military stores and grain, and destroyed the walls before withdrawing.

sentences.zh: 又攻玉門軍及常樂縣，縣令賈師順嬰城固守，賊遂引退。

translations.literal: They again attacked Yumen Army and Changle County; Magistrate Jia Shishun closed the city and held firm, and the bandits then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: They also attacked Yumen Army and Changle County, but Magistrate Jia Shishun held the walls firm and the enemy withdrew.

sentences.zh: 無何，君滷又為回紇諸部殺之於鞏筆驛，河、隴震駭。

translations.literal: Before long Junyao was also killed by various Uyghur tribes at Gongbi Post; the He and Long regions were shaken with alarm.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Junyao was killed by Uyghur tribes at Gongbi Post, sending shock through the He and Long frontier regions.

sentences.zh: 玄宗以君滷勇將無謀，果及於難，擇堪邊任者，乃以嵩為兵部尚書、河西節度使，判涼州事。

translations.literal: Xuanzong considered that Junyao, a brave general without strategy, had indeed met with disaster; selecting one fit for frontier duty, he made Song Minister of War and Military Commissioner of Hexi, with authority over Liang affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong judged that Junyao, a brave but unstrategic general, had brought disaster on himself; he selected Song as Minister of War and Military Commissioner of Hexi, with authority over Liangzhou affairs.

sentences.zh: 嵩乃請以裴寬、郭虛己、牛仙客在其幕下，又請以建康軍使、左金吾將軍張守珪為瓜州刺史，修築州城，招輯百姓，令其復業。

translations.literal: Song thereupon requested Pei Kuan, Guo Xuji, and Niu Xianke in his staff, and also requested Jiankang Army Commissioner and Left General of the Golden Guards Zhang Shougui as prefect of Gua, to repair the prefectural walls, gather and settle the people, and have them resume their occupations.
translations.idiomatic: Song requested Pei Kuan, Guo Xuji, and Niu Xianke for his staff, and asked that Zhang Shougui, commissioner of the Jiankang Army and Left General of the Golden Guards, be made prefect of Guazhou to rebuild the city walls, gather the populace, and restore their livelihoods.

sentences.zh: 又加嵩銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Song was further given Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: Song was further promoted to Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 時悉諾邏恭祿威名甚振，嵩乃縱反間於吐蕃，言其與中國潛通，贊普遂召而誅之。

translations.literal: At that time Sinoluogonglu's reputation was greatly ascendant; Song therefore spread discord among the Tibetans, saying he had secret communication with China, and the tsenpo summoned and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Sinoluogonglu's reputation was then at its height; Song spread disinformation among the Tibetans that he was secretly communicating with China, and the Tibetan ruler summoned and executed him.

sentences.zh: 明年秋，吐蕃大下，悉末明復率眾攻瓜州，守珪出兵擊走之。

translations.literal: The next autumn the Tibetans came down in force; Ximoming again led troops to attack Gua; Shougui sent troops and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: The following autumn Tibet invaded in force; Ximoming again led troops against Guazhou, but Shougui drove them off.

sentences.zh: 隴右節度使、鄯州都督張誌亮引兵至青海西南馮波谷，與吐蕃接戰，大破之。

translations.literal: Military Commissioner of Longyou and Area Commander of Shan Zhang Zhiliang led troops to Fengbo Valley southwest of Qinghai, engaged the Tibetans, and routed them greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhiliang, Military Commissioner of Longyou and Area Commander of Shanzhou, led troops to Fengbo Valley southwest of Qinghai, engaged the Tibetans, and won a great victory.

sentences.zh: 八月，嵩又遣副將杜賓客率弩手四千人，與吐蕃戰於祁連城下，自晨至暮，散而復合，賊徒大潰，臨陣斬其副將一人，散走山谷，哭聲四合。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Song again sent Vice General Du Binke leading four thousand crossbowmen to battle the Tibetans below Qilian Fortress; from morning to evening they scattered and re-formed; the bandits were greatly routed; one of their vice generals was beheaded on the field; they scattered into the valleys and ravines, and cries of grief sounded on all sides.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Song sent Vice General Du Binke with four thousand crossbowmen to fight the Tibetans below Qilian Fortress. The battle raged from morning to evening; the enemy broke and re-formed repeatedly, then collapsed in rout. One Tibetan vice general was beheaded on the field; the survivors fled into the valleys wailing on all sides.

sentences.zh: 露布至，玄宗大悅，乃加嵩同中書門下三品，恩顧莫比。

translations.literal: When the victory bulletin arrived, Xuanzong was greatly pleased and added Song as Associate of the Third Rank of the Secretariat-Chancellery; his favor was unmatched.
translations.idiomatic: When the victory bulletin arrived Xuanzong was delighted and made Song Associate of the Third Rank of the Secretariat-Chancellery; his favor was unmatched.

sentences.zh: 十七年，授宇文融、裴光庭宰相，又加嵩兼中書令。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year Yuwen Rong and Pei Guangting were made chief ministers, and Song was further made concurrent Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In 729 Yuwen Rong and Pei Guangting were appointed chief ministers, and Song was further made concurrent Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 自十四年燕國公張說罷中書令後，缺此位四年，而嵩居之。

translations.literal: Since the fourteenth year when Duke of Yan Zhang Yue left the post of Director of the Secretariat, this position had been vacant four years, and Song now held it.
translations.idiomatic: Since Zhang Yue, Duke of Yan, had left the post of Director of the Secretariat in 726, the office had been vacant for four years; Song now filled it.

sentences.zh: 常帶河西節度，遙領之。

translations.literal: He constantly retained the Hexi commission and held it at a distance.
translations.idiomatic: He continued to hold the Hexi commission in absentia.

sentences.zh: 加集賢殿學士、知院事，兼修國史，進位金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He was given Academician of the Jixian Hall and charge of academy affairs, concurrently editing the national history, and advanced to Golden-Gleaming Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Academician of the Jixian Hall with charge of academy affairs, concurrently editor of the national history, and promoted to Golden-Gleaming Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 子衡，尚新昌公主，嵩夫人賀氏入覲拜席，玄宗呼為親家母，禮儀甚盛。

translations.literal: His son Heng married Princess Xinchang; Song's wife Lady He entered audience and bowed at the feast; Xuanzong called her mother-in-law by marriage, and the ceremonial was very grand.
translations.idiomatic: His son Heng married Princess Xinchang; when Song's wife Lady He attended court and bowed at the feast, Xuanzong addressed her as his mother-in-law by marriage with great ceremony.

sentences.zh: 尋又進封徐國公。

translations.literal: Before long he was further enfeoffed as Duke of Xu.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon further enfeoffed as Duke of Xu.

sentences.zh: 二十一年二月，侍中裴光庭卒。

translations.literal: In the second month of the twenty-first year Attending Secretariat Director Pei Guangting died.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of 733 Attending Secretariat Director Pei Guangting died.

sentences.zh: 光庭與嵩同位數年，情頗不協，及是，玄宗遣嵩擇相，嵩以右丞韓休長者，舉之。

translations.literal: Guangting and Song had shared rank several years and their feelings were quite incompatible; at this point Xuanzong sent Song to select a chief minister; Song, considering Right Vice Director Han Xiu a man of mature years, recommended him.
translations.idiomatic: Guangting and Song had shared power for years on poor terms; the Emperor now asked Song to recommend a successor. Song nominated Han Xiu, the Right Vice Director, as a man of mature judgment.

sentences.zh: 及休入相，嵩舉事，休峭直，輒不相假，互於玄宗前論曲直，因讓位。

translations.literal: When Xiu entered the chancellorship, Song raised affairs; Xiu was stern and upright and would not yield to him; they argued right and wrong before Xuanzong, and Song thereupon yielded his post.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Xiu became chief minister he was stern and upright and would not defer to Song; they argued before the Emperor until Song offered to resign.

sentences.zh: 玄宗眷嵩厚，乃許嵩授尚書右丞相，令罷相，以休為工部尚書。

translations.literal: Xuanzong's favor for Song was thick; he therefore permitted Song to be given Right Chancellor of the Department of State Affairs, ordered him to cease being chief minister, and made Xiu Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor's affection for Song remained strong; he permitted Song to take the title Right Chancellor of the Department of State Affairs while leaving the chancellorship, and made Han Xiu Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 尋又以嵩子華為給事中。

translations.literal: Before long he also made Song's son Hua a Drafting Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He soon appointed Song's son Hua as Drafting Attendant.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，拜太子太師。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he was appointed Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In 736 he was appointed Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 及幽州節度使張守珪坐賂遺中官牛仙童，貶為括州刺史，嵩嘗賄仙童，李林甫發之，貶青州刺史。

translations.literal: When Military Commissioner of You Zhang Shougui, for bribing the eunuch Niu Xiantong, was demoted to prefect of Kuo, Song had once bribed Xiantong; Li Linfu exposed this, and he was demoted to prefect of Qing.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Shougui, Military Commissioner of Youzhou, was demoted to prefect of Kuozhou for bribing the eunuch Niu Xiantong, Li Linfu exposed Song's own bribery of Xiantong, and Song was demoted to prefect of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 尋又追拜太子太師，嵩又請老。

translations.literal: Before long he was again appointed Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent; Song again requested retirement on account of age.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon reappointed Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, but Song again petitioned to retire.

sentences.zh: 嵩性好服餌，及罷相，於林園植藥，合煉自適。

translations.literal: Song by nature loved taking medicines and elixirs; when he left the chancellorship he planted drugs in his woodland garden and compounded and refined them for his own pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: Song loved taking medicines and elixirs; after leaving office he planted herbs in his garden and compounded them for his own use.

sentences.zh: 華時為工部侍郎，衡以主婿三品，嵩皤然就養十餘年，家財豐贍，衣冠榮之。

translations.literal: Hua was then Vice Minister of Works; Heng, as the emperor's son-in-law, held third rank; Song, white-haired, received support for more than ten years; the family wealth was abundant, and the gentry honored them.
translations.idiomatic: Hua was then Vice Minister of Works; Heng, as the emperor's son-in-law, held third rank. Song lived in white-haired retirement for more than ten years, his household wealthy and honored among the gentry.

sentences.zh: 天寶八年薨，年八十餘，贈開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Tianbao he died, aged more than eighty; he was posthumously made Grand Master of the Palace with the same ceremonial as the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 749 at more than eighty years of age and was posthumously made Grand Master of the Palace with ceremonial equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 蕭華子華，天寶末轉兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: Xiao Hua, Song's son Hua, at the end of Tianbao was transferred to Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Hua was transferred to Vice Minister of War at the end of the Tianbao era.

sentences.zh: 祿山之亂，從駕不及，陷賊，偽署魏州刺史。

translations.literal: In the An Lushan rebellion he could not follow the imperial carriage in time, fell into the rebels' hands, and was falsely appointed prefect of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: During the An Lushan rebellion he failed to accompany the court in its flight, fell into rebel hands, and was appointed prefect of Weizhou under the rebel regime.

sentences.zh: 乾元元年，郭子儀與九節度之師渡河攻安慶緒於相州，華潛通表疏，俟官軍至為內應。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianyuan Guo Ziyi and the armies of the nine commissioners crossed the river to attack An Qingxu at Xiang; Hua secretly communicated memorials and tables, waiting for the official army to arrive to act as inner response.
translations.idiomatic: In 758 Guo Ziyi and the armies of the nine commissioners crossed the Yellow River to attack An Qingxu at Xiangzhou; Hua secretly sent memorials pledging to serve as an inside collaborator when the imperial army arrived.

sentences.zh: 賊伺知之，禁錮華於獄。

translations.literal: The rebels detected this and imprisoned Hua in jail.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels discovered his plot and imprisoned him.

sentences.zh: 崔光遠收魏州，破械出華。

translations.literal: Cui Guangyuan recovered Wei Prefecture, broke his fetters, and released Hua.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Guangyuan recovered Weizhou, broke his chains, and freed him.

sentences.zh: 魏人美華之惠政，詣光遠請留，朝廷正授魏州刺史。

translations.literal: The people of Wei admired Hua's benevolent governance and went to Guangyuan requesting he remain; the court formally appointed him prefect of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Wei admired his benevolent administration and petitioned Guangyuan to retain him; the court formally appointed him prefect of Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 既而史思明率眾南下，子儀懼華復陷，乃表崔光遠代華，召至軍中。

translations.literal: Before long Shi Siming led troops south; Ziyi feared Hua would again fall into captivity and therefore memorialized Cui Guangyuan to replace Hua and summoned him to the army.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Shi Siming led his forces south; Guo Ziyi feared Hua would be captured again and memorialized for Cui Guangyuan to replace him, summoning Hua to headquarters.

sentences.zh: 及相州兵潰，華歸京，仍以偽命所汙，降授試秘書少監。

translations.literal: When the army collapsed at Xiang, Hua returned to the capital; because he was still tainted by the false appointment, he was demoted and given provisional Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: After the rout at Xiangzhou Hua returned to the capital but, still tainted by his service under the rebels, was demoted to provisional Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 華謹重方雅，綽有家法，人士稱之。

translations.literal: Hua was careful, weighty, square, and refined, with ample family discipline; gentlemen praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Hua was careful, dignified, and refined, with strong family discipline; men of standing praised him.

sentences.zh: 尋遷尚書右丞。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 乾元二年，出為河中尹、河中晉絳節度使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qianyuan he went out as Governor of Hezhong and Military Commissioner of Hezhong, Jin, and Jiang.
translations.idiomatic: In 759 he was sent out as Governor of Hezhong and Military Commissioner of Hezhong, Jin, and Jiang.

sentences.zh: 上元元年十二月，制曰：「弼予之選，審象是求，天步未平，廟謨尤切。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the first year of Shangyuan an edict stated: "In choosing one to assist me, I seek one who examines the signs; the heavenly steps are not yet level, and the temple stratagems are especially urgent.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of 760 an edict declared: "In choosing one to assist me, I seek one who reads the signs of the times; the realm is not yet pacified, and statecraft is urgently needed.

sentences.zh: 必資明表，佇以佐時，畫一之才，取則不遠。

translations.literal: I must rely on a bright exemplar, waiting to aid the age; talent for unifying policy—one to take as model is not far.
translations.idiomatic: I require a brilliant exemplar to aid the age; talent to unify policy is close at hand.

sentences.zh: 正議大夫、前河中尹、兼御史中丞、充本府晉絳等州節度觀察等使、上柱國、嗣徐國公、賜紫金魚袋蕭華，公輔成名，承家繼業，詞標麗則，德蘊謨明。

translations.literal: Proper Counselor Xiao Hua, former Governor of Hezhong, concurrently Vice Censor-in-Chief, fulfilling this office's commission as Military Commissioner and Observation Commissioner of Jin, Jiang, and other prefectures, Pillar of the State, heir to the Duke of Xu, granted the gold and purple fish bag: his fame as chief minister is established, he inherits the family enterprise, his words mark beautiful standards, his virtue contains clear strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Proper Counselor Xiao Hua, former Governor of Hezhong, concurrently Vice Censor-in-Chief and Military Commissioner of Jin and Jiang prefectures, Pillar of the State, heir to the Duke of Xu, bearer of the gold and purple fish tally: renowned as a chief minister, heir to a distinguished house, his words elegant and his virtue steeped in wise counsel.

sentences.zh: 再履宮坊，尤知至行，致君望美，閱相求能。

translations.literal: Twice treading the palace wards, he especially knows utmost conduct; in serving the ruler he looks to beauty; in reviewing chief ministers he seeks ability.
translations.idiomatic: Twice serving in the palace administration, he knows utmost conduct well; in serving the ruler he aspires to excellence; in reviewing ministers he seeks true ability.

sentences.zh: 且推伊陟之賢，更啟漢臣之閤，還依日月，佐理陰陽。

translations.literal: Moreover, he extends the worth of Yi Zhi, again opens the gate of Han ministers, returns to rely on sun and moon, and assists in ordering yin and yang.
translations.idiomatic: He extends the worth of Yi Zhi, reopens the gate of Han ministers, returns to stand beside the sun and moon, and assists in ordering the realm.

sentences.zh: 俾參政於紫宸，用建中於皇極。

translations.literal: Let him participate in government at the Purple Asterism Hall and employ the Mean to establish the supreme pole.
translations.idiomatic: Let him take part in government at the Purple Asterism Hall and employ the Mean to establish the supreme pole.

sentences.zh: 可中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事、集賢殿崇文館大學士，監修國史。」

translations.literal: He is fit to be Vice Director of the Secretariat, Associate Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery, Grand Academician of the Jixian and Chongwen Halls, and supervisor of editing the national history."
translations.idiomatic: He is appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat, Associate Chief Minister, Grand Academician of the Jixian and Chongwen Halls, and supervisor of editing the national history."

sentences.zh: 時中官李輔國專典禁兵，怙寵用事，求為宰相，諷宰臣裴冕等薦己，華頗拒之，輔國怒。

translations.literal: At that time the eunuch Li Fuguo exclusively controlled the forbidden troops, relied on favor to wield power, sought to become chief minister, and hinted to chief ministers Pei Mian and others to recommend him; Hua considerably refused, and Fuguo was angry.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Li Fuguo then controlled the palace guard, wielded power through imperial favor, and sought the chancellorship, pressuring chief ministers such as Pei Mian to recommend him. Hua resisted firmly, and Fuguo was enraged.

sentences.zh: 肅宗方寢疾，輔國矯命罷華相位，守禮部尚書，仍引元載代華。

translations.literal: Suzong was then ill in bed; Fuguo forged an order removing Hua from the chancellorship, retaining him as Minister of Rites, and still brought in Yuan Zai to replace Hua.
translations.idiomatic: While Emperor Suzong lay ill, Fuguo forged an order removing Hua from the chancellorship and retaining him as Minister of Rites, then installed Yuan Zai in his place.

sentences.zh: 肅宗崩，代宗在諒暗，元載希輔國旨，貶華為硤州員外司馬，卒於貶所。

translations.literal: When Suzong died, Daizong was in mourning seclusion; Yuan Zai, hoping to please Fuguo, demoted Hua to Extraordinary Acting Military Adjutant of Xia Prefecture, and he died at his place of exile.
translations.idiomatic: After Suzong's death, while Daizong was in mourning seclusion, Yuan Zai, courting Fuguo's favor, demoted Hua to acting military adjutant of Xiazhou; he died in exile.

sentences.zh: 蕭衡、蕭華後人衡子復，德宗朝位亦至宰輔。

translations.literal: Among the later descendants of Xiao Heng and Xiao Hua, Heng's son Fu in Dezong's reign also reached the rank of chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Among the later descendants of Xiao Heng and Xiao Hua, Heng's son Fu rose to chief minister under Emperor Dezong.

sentences.zh: 華子恆、悟。

translations.literal: Hua's sons were Heng and Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Hua's sons were Heng and Wu.

sentences.zh: 恆子俯，大和中宰輔。

translations.literal: Heng's son Fu became chief minister in the Dahe era.
translations.idiomatic: Heng's son Fu became chief minister in the Dahe era (827–835).

sentences.zh: 悟子仿，咸通中宰輔，皆自有傳。

translations.literal: Wu's son Fang became chief minister in the Xiantong era; each has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Wu's son Fang became chief minister in the Xiantong era (860–874); each has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 張九齡，字子壽，一名博物。

translations.literal: Zhang Jiuling, style name Zishou, with another name Bowu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jiuling, style name Zishou, also known as Bowu.

sentences.zh: 曾祖君政，韶州別駕，因家於始興，今為曲江人。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Junzheng was Vice Prefect of Shao and on that account made his home at Shixing; he is now counted as a man of Qujiang.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Junzheng was Vice Prefect of Shaozhou and settled the family at Shixing; the clan is now counted as from Qujiang.

sentences.zh: 父弘愈，以九齡貴，贈廣州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Hongyu, because of Jiuling's eminence, was posthumously made prefect of Guang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Hongyu was posthumously made prefect of Guangzhou because of Jiuling's eminence.

sentences.zh: 九齡幼聰敏，善屬文。

translations.literal: Jiuling was clever and perceptive in youth and skilled at literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: Jiuling was clever and perceptive as a boy and skilled at literary composition.

sentences.zh: 年十三，以書幹廣州刺史王方慶，大嗟賞之，曰：「此子必能致遠。」

translations.literal: At thirteen he presented a letter to Guang Prefect Wang Fangqing, who greatly admired him and said: "This youth is sure to reach far.
translations.idiomatic: At thirteen he presented a letter to Guangzhou Prefect Wang Fangqing, who greatly admired him and said, "This youth is bound to go far."

sentences.zh: 登進士第，應舉登乙第，拜校書郎。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination, entered the special examination at the second grade, and was appointed Collator.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination, earned the second grade in the special examination, and was appointed Collator.

sentences.zh: 玄宗在東宮，舉天下文藻之士，親加策問，九齡對策高第，遷右拾遺。

translations.literal: When Xuanzong was in the Eastern Palace he gathered literary talents from all under Heaven and personally examined them by policy questions; Jiuling answered at the top grade and was transferred to Right Reminder.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzong was crown prince he gathered literary talents from across the empire and personally examined them; Jiuling ranked at the top and was promoted to Right Reminder.

sentences.zh: 時帝未行親郊之禮，九齡上疏曰：伏以天才者，百神之君，而王者之所由受命也。自古繼統之主，必有郊配之義，蓋以敬天命以報所受。故於郊之義，則不以德澤未洽，年谷不登，凡事之故，而闕其禮。《孝經》云：「昔者周公郊祀後稷以配天。」斯謂成王幼沖，周公居攝，猶用其禮，明不暫廢。漢丞相匡衡亦云：「帝王之事，莫重乎郊祀。」董仲舒又云：「不郊而祭山川，失祭之序，逆於禮正，故《春秋》非之。」臣愚以為匡衡、仲舒，古之知禮者，皆謂郊之為祭所宜先也。伏惟陛下紹休聖緒，其命惟新，御極已來，於今五載，既光太平之業，未行大報之禮，竊考經傳，義或未通。今百穀嘉生，鳥獸咸若，夷狄內附，兵革用寧。將欲鑄劍為農，泥金封禪，用彰功德之美，允答神只之心。能事畢行，光耀帝載。況郊祀常典，猶闕其儀，有若怠於事天，臣恐不可以訓。伏望以迎日之至，展焚柴之禮，升紫壇，陳采席，定天位，明天道，則聖朝典則，可謂無遺矣。

translations.literal: At that time the Emperor had not yet personally performed the suburban sacrifice, and Jiuling submitted a memorial, saying: I humbly submit that Heaven is the lord of the hundred spirits and that by which kings receive the Mandate. From antiquity, rulers who have succeeded to the line have necessarily had the principle of the suburban sacrifice and matching ancestor, because they revere Heaven's Mandate and repay what they have received. Thus, in the meaning of the suburban sacrifice, the rite is not omitted because virtue and grace have not yet spread widely, because the yearly grain has not ripened, or because of ordinary affairs. The Classic of Filial Piety says, "Formerly the Duke of Zhou performed the suburban sacrifice to Hou Ji to match Heaven."
