This refers to when King Cheng was young and the Duke of Zhou held the regency, yet he still used this rite, making clear that it was not to be suspended even temporarily. Kuang Heng, Chancellor of Han, also said, "Among the affairs of emperors and kings, none is more important than the suburban sacrifice." Dong Zhongshu also said, "To sacrifice to mountains and rivers without performing the suburban sacrifice loses the order of sacrifice and goes against ritual correctness; therefore the Spring and Autumn censures it." In your subject's foolish view, Kuang Heng and Zhongshu were men of antiquity who understood ritual, and both held that, among sacrifices, the suburban sacrifice should come first. I humbly think that Your Majesty has inherited the splendid sacred line and that the Mandate is newly renewed. Since you ascended the throne, five years have now passed; you have already glorified the work of great peace, but have not yet performed the great rite of repayment. When I privately examine the classics and commentaries, the principle may not be fully coherent. Now the hundred grains grow beautifully, birds and beasts all accord with order, barbarians have submitted inwardly, and weapons and armor are at peace. You are about to cast swords into farming tools and seal with mud in the Feng and Shan sacrifices, thereby displaying the beauty of merit and virtue and truly answering the hearts of the spirits. All possible affairs have been carried out, shining over the imperial record. Yet if the constant canon of the suburban sacrifice still lacks its ceremony, it seems like negligence in serving Heaven, and your subject fears it cannot serve as instruction. I humbly hope that at the arrival of the day for greeting the sun, you will set out the rite of burning firewood, ascend the purple altar, arrange the colored mats, fix the place of Heaven, and make clear the Way of Heaven. Then the statutes and models of the sacred court may be called without omission.

sentences.zh: 九齡以才鑒見推，當時吏部試拔萃選人及應舉者，咸令九齡與右拾遺趙冬曦考其等第，前後數四，每稱平允。

translations.literal: Jiuling was recommended for his talent and discernment; at that time for the Ministry of Personnel's examination of outstanding candidates and examination entrants, all were ordered to have Jiuling and Right Reminder Zhao Dongxi grade their ranks; this happened four times in succession, and each time he was called fair and even.
translations.idiomatic: Jiuling was esteemed for his talent and discernment. The Ministry of Personnel repeatedly assigned him and Right Reminder Zhao Dongxi to grade candidates for the outstanding selection and civil examinations; they did so four times in succession, and each time their judgments were praised as fair.

sentences.zh: 開元十年，三遷司勛員外郎。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Kaiyuan, after three promotions he became Vice Director of the Bureau of Merit.
translations.idiomatic: In 722, after three promotions, he became Vice Director of the Bureau of Merit.

sentences.zh: 時張說為中書令，與九齡同姓，敘為昭穆，尤親重之，常謂人曰：「後來詞人稱首也。」

translations.literal: At that time Zhang Yue was Director of the Secretariat; he shared a surname with Jiuling and arranged their kinship as elder and younger branches, especially cherishing him, and often told people: "Among later men of letters he is foremost.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yue was then Director of the Secretariat; he shared Jiuling's surname and treated him as a kinsman of the younger generation, cherishing him greatly and often saying, "Among later men of letters he stands first."

sentences.zh: 九齡既欣知己，亦依附焉。

translations.literal: Jiuling, delighted at finding a confidant, also attached himself to him.
translations.idiomatic: Jiuling, delighted to find a patron, attached himself to Yue as well.

sentences.zh: 十一年，拜中書舍人。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was appointed Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: In 723 he was appointed Secretariat Drafter.

sentences.zh: 十三年，車駕東巡，行封禪之禮。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year the imperial carriage toured east and performed the feng and shan rites.
translations.idiomatic: In 725 the Emperor traveled east and performed the feng and shan sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 說自定侍從升中之官，多引兩省錄事主書及己之所親攝官而上，遂加特進階，超授五品。

translations.literal: Yue himself fixed the attendants' posts for ascending Mount Tai, largely bringing up recording clerks and chief clerks of the two secretariats and his own intimates acting in office, and then specially advanced them in rank, leap-promoting them to fifth grade.
translations.idiomatic: Yue himself fixed the posts for attendants at the Mount Tai ascent, promoting many recording clerks and chief clerks from the two secretariats and his own intimates acting in office, then specially advancing them and leap-promoting them to fifth rank.

sentences.zh: 初，令九齡草詔，九齡言於說曰：「官爵者，天下之公器，德望為先，勞舊次焉。

translations.literal: At first Yue ordered Jiuling to draft the edict; Jiuling said to Yue: "Office and rank are the public vessels of the realm; virtue and reputation come first, merit and seniority next.
translations.idiomatic: Yue first ordered Jiuling to draft the edict. Jiuling told him, "Office and rank are the public vessels of the realm; virtue and reputation come first, merit and seniority next.

sentences.zh: 若顛倒衣裳，則譏謗起矣。

translations.literal: If you turn garments upside down, ridicule and slander will arise.
translations.idiomatic: If ranks are turned upside down, ridicule and slander will follow.

sentences.zh: 今登封霈澤，千載一遇。

translations.literal: Now the feng sacrifice's generous favor is a meeting once in a thousand years.
translations.idiomatic: The blessings of the feng sacrifice come once in a thousand years.

sentences.zh: 清流高品，不沐殊恩。

translations.literal: The clear current and high grades do not bathe in special grace.
translations.idiomatic: Men of pure reputation and high rank receive no special grace,

sentences.zh: 胥吏末班，先加章紱。

translations.literal: while clerks of the lowest ranks are first given insignia and ribbons.
translations.idiomatic: while clerks of the lowest ranks are first given insignia and ribbons.

sentences.zh: 但恐制出之後，四方失望。

translations.literal: I fear only that after the edict is issued, the four quarters will be disappointed.
translations.idiomatic: I fear that once the edict is issued, the empire will be disappointed.

sentences.zh: 今進草之際，事猶可改，唯令公審籌之，無貽後悔也。」

translations.literal: Now in submitting the draft the matter can still be changed; I only beg Your Excellency to consider it carefully and leave no cause for regret.
translations.idiomatic: The draft can still be revised. I beg Your Excellency to consider carefully and leave no cause for regret."

sentences.zh: 說曰：「事已決矣，悠悠之談，何足慮也！」

translations.literal: Yue said: "The matter is already decided; idle talk—what is there to worry about!"
translations.idiomatic: Yue replied, "The matter is settled. Idle talk is not worth worrying about!"

sentences.zh: 竟不從。

translations.literal: In the end he did not follow his advice.
translations.idiomatic: He did not heed the advice.

sentences.zh: 及制出，內外甚咎於說。

translations.literal: When the edict was issued, inside and outside greatly blamed Yue.
translations.idiomatic: When the edict was issued, court and country alike blamed Yue.

sentences.zh: 時御史中丞宇文融方知田戶之事，每有所奏，說多建議違之，融亦以此不平於說。

translations.literal: At that time Vice Censor-in-Chief Yuwen Rong had just mastered matters of field households; whenever he memorialized, Yue often proposed contrary measures, and Rong on this account was also resentful toward Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Censor-in-Chief Yuwen Rong had just mastered the field-household system; whenever he memorialized, Yue often opposed him, and Rong grew resentful.

sentences.zh: 九齡復勸說為備，說又不從其言。

translations.literal: Jiuling again urged Yue to take precautions; Yue again did not follow his words.
translations.idiomatic: Jiuling again urged Yue to take precautions; Yue again refused.

sentences.zh: 無幾，說果為融所劾，罷知政事，九齡亦改太常少卿，尋出為冀暫刺史。

translations.literal: Before long Yue was indeed impeached by Rong, ceased participating in government, Jiuling was also changed to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and soon went out as prefect of Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Yue was impeached by Rong and left office; Jiuling was transferred to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and soon sent out as prefect of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 九齡以母老在鄉，而河北道里遼遠，上疏固請換江南一州，望得數承母音耗，優制許之，改為洪州都督。

translations.literal: Jiuling, because his mother was old in the home district and the Hebei route was distant, memorialized firmly requesting exchange for a Jiangnan prefecture, hoping to receive news of his mother several times; a gracious edict granted this and changed him to Area Commander of Hong.
translations.idiomatic: Jiuling's mother was elderly in their home district, and the Hebei posting was far away; he memorialized firmly to exchange it for a Jiangnan prefecture so he could hear from her more often. The Emperor graciously agreed and made him Area Commander of Hongzhou.

sentences.zh: 俄轉桂州都督，仍充嶺南道按察使。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to Area Commander of Gui and still served as Investigation Commissioner of the Lingnan Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to Area Commander of Guizhou and also served as Investigation Commissioner of the Lingnan Circuit.

sentences.zh: 上又以其弟九章、九臯為嶺南道刺史，令歲時伏臘，皆得寧覲。

translations.literal: The Emperor also made his younger brothers Jiuzhang and Jiugao prefects on the Lingnan Circuit, so that at seasonal festivals they could all pay peaceful visits.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor also appointed his younger brothers Jiuzhang and Jiugao as prefects on the Lingnan Circuit so that at seasonal festivals they could all visit their mother in peace.

sentences.zh: 初，張說知集賢院事，常薦九齡堪為學士，以備顧問。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Zhang Yue directed Jixian Academy affairs, he often recommended Jiuling as fit to be an academician to supply consultation.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Yue directed the Jixian Academy he often recommended Jiuling as fit to be an academician and imperial adviser.

sentences.zh: 說卒後，上思其言，召拜九齡為秘書少監、集賢院學士，副知院事。

translations.literal: After Yue died the Emperor recalled his words and summoned Jiuling to be appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat Library, Jixian Academician, and deputy director of academy affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After Yue's death the Emperor recalled his recommendation and appointed Jiuling Vice Director of the Secretariat Library, Jixian Academician, and deputy director of academy affairs.

sentences.zh: 再遷中書侍郎。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 常密有陳奏，多見納用。

translations.literal: He often had confidential memorials, many of which were adopted.
translations.idiomatic: He often submitted confidential memorials, many of which the Emperor adopted.

sentences.zh: 尋丁母喪歸鄉里。

translations.literal: Before long he mourned his mother's death and returned to his home district.
translations.idiomatic: He soon mourned his mother's death and returned home.

sentences.zh: 二十一年十二月，起復拜中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the twenty-first year he was recalled from mourning and appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat and Associate Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of 733 he was recalled from mourning and appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat and Associate Chief Minister.

sentences.zh: 明年，遷中書令，兼修國史。

translations.literal: The next year he was transferred to Director of the Secretariat and concurrently edited the national history.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was promoted to Director of the Secretariat and concurrently editor of the national history.

sentences.zh: 時范陽節度使張守珪以裨將安祿山討奚、契丹敗衄，執送京師，請行朝典。

translations.literal: At that time Military Commissioner of Fanyang Zhang Shougui, because his lieutenant An Lushan in campaigning against the Xi and Khitan suffered defeat, seized and sent him to the capital, requesting application of court law.
translations.idiomatic: Military Commissioner of Fanyang Zhang Shougui had his lieutenant An Lushan campaign against the Xi and Khitan; when Lushan was defeated, Shougui seized him and sent him to the capital, requesting that court law be applied.

sentences.zh: 九齡奏劾曰：「穰苴出軍，必誅莊賈；

translations.literal: Jiuling memorialized impeachment: "When Rangju led the army out, he was sure to execute Zhuang Jia;
translations.idiomatic: Jiuling memorialized: "When Rangju led the army forth, he executed Zhuang Jia;

sentences.zh: 孫武教戰，亦斬宮嬪。

translations.literal: when Sun Wu taught warfare, he also beheaded palace women.
translations.idiomatic: when Sun Wu taught warfare, he beheaded palace women as well.

sentences.zh: 守珪軍令必行，祿山不宜免死。」

translations.literal: Shougui's military orders must be enforced; Lushan should not be spared death.
translations.idiomatic: Shougui's military orders must be enforced; Lushan ought not be spared death."

sentences.zh: 上特舍之。

translations.literal: The Emperor specially pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor specially pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 九齡奏曰：「祿山狼子野心，面有逆相，臣請因罪戮之，冀絕後患。」

translations.literal: Jiuling memorialized: "Lushan has the heart of a wolf cub and the face of a rebel; I beg to execute him for his crime, hoping to cut off later trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Jiuling said, "Lushan has the heart of a wolf cub and the face of a rebel. I beg to execute him for his crime and forestall future trouble."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「卿勿以王夷甫知石勒故事，誤害忠良。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Do not, like Wang Yifu recognizing Shi Le's story, mistakenly harm the loyal and good."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor replied, "Do not, like Wang Yifu who recognized Shi Le too late, mistakenly harm a loyal man."

sentences.zh: 遂放歸籓。

translations.literal: He was therefore released and returned to the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Lushan was released and sent back to the frontier.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，加金紫光祿大夫，累封始興縣伯。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he was given Golden-Gleaming Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and enfeoffed in succession as Earl of Shixing County.
translations.idiomatic: In 735 he was made Golden-Gleaming Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and enfeoffed as Earl of Shixing County.

sentences.zh: 李林甫自無學術，以九齡文行為上所知，心頗忌之。

translations.literal: Li Linfu himself lacked learning; because Jiuling's literary conduct was known to the Emperor, he was rather jealous in heart.
translations.idiomatic: Li Linfu lacked learning himself and resented that the Emperor valued Jiuling's literary conduct and integrity.

sentences.zh: 乃引牛仙客知政事，九齡屢言不可，帝不悅。

translations.literal: He therefore brought in Niu Xianke to participate in government; Jiuling repeatedly said this was not permissible, and the Emperor was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: He brought Niu Xianke into government; Jiuling repeatedly objected, and the Emperor was displeased.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，遷尚書右丞相，罷知政事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he was transferred to Right Chancellor of the Department of State Affairs and ceased participating in government.
translations.idiomatic: In 736 he was transferred to Right Chancellor of the Department of State Affairs and left the chancellorship.

sentences.zh: 後宰執每薦引公卿，上必問：「風度得如九齡否？」

translations.literal: Later whenever chief ministers recommended and introduced high officials, the Emperor always asked: "Does his bearing match Jiuling's?
translations.idiomatic: Whenever chief ministers later recommended high officials, the Emperor always asked, "Does his bearing match Jiuling's?"

sentences.zh: 故事皆搢笏於帶，而後乘馬，九齡體羸，常使人持之，因設笏囊。

translations.literal: By precedent all tucked the court tablet in the belt before mounting a horse; Jiuling's body was frail and he often had someone hold it, and on this account the tablet pouch was devised.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent officials tucked their court tablets in their belts before mounting a horse. Jiuling's health was frail, and he often had an attendant carry his tablet; he therefore devised the tablet pouch.

sentences.zh: 笏囊之設，自九齡始也。

translations.literal: The establishment of the tablet pouch began with Jiuling.
translations.idiomatic: The tablet pouch began with Jiuling.

sentences.zh: 初，九齡為相，薦長安尉周子諒為監察御史。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Jiuling was chief minister, he recommended Chang'an Vice Magistrate Zhou Ziliang as investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiuling was chief minister he had recommended Chang'an Vice Magistrate Zhou Ziliang as investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 至是，子諒以妄陳休咎，上親加詰問，令於朝堂決殺之。

translations.literal: At this point Ziliang, for rashly stating omens of fortune and calamity, was personally interrogated by the Emperor and ordered executed by decision at court.
translations.idiomatic: Ziliang then rashly predicted fortune and calamity; the Emperor personally interrogated him and ordered his execution at court.

sentences.zh: 九齡坐引非其人，左遷荊州大都督府長史。

translations.literal: Jiuling, for having introduced an unfit person, was transferred left to Senior Administrator of the Jing Metropolitan Command.
translations.idiomatic: Jiuling was demoted to Senior Administrator of the Jingzhou Metropolitan Command for having recommended an unfit man.

sentences.zh: 俄請歸拜墓，因遇疾卒，年六十八，贈荊州大都督，謚曰文獻。

translations.literal: Before long he requested return to pay respects at the tomb; he then encountered illness and died, aged sixty-eight; he was posthumously made Metropolitan Governor of Jing, with the posthumous title Wenxian.
translations.idiomatic: He soon requested leave to visit his parents' tombs, fell ill on the journey, and died at sixty-eight. He was posthumously made Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhou and given the posthumous title Wenxian ("Literary Exemplar").

sentences.zh: 九齡在相位時，建議復置十道采訪使，又教河南數州水種稻，以廣屯田。

translations.literal: When Jiuling was in the chancellorship he proposed restoring the ten-circuit investigation commissioners and also taught several Henan prefectures to plant rice by water in order to expand garrison fields.
translations.idiomatic: As chief minister Jiuling proposed restoring the ten-circuit investigation commissioners and urged several Henan prefectures to plant rice by irrigation to expand garrison agriculture.

sentences.zh: 議置屯田，費功無利，竟不能就，罷之。

translations.literal: The proposal to establish garrison fields cost labor without profit and in the end could not be completed; it was abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison-field project cost labor without profit and was eventually abandoned.

sentences.zh: 性頗躁急，動輒忿詈，議者以此少之。

translations.literal: His nature was rather impatient and hasty; he would readily burst into angry abuse; commentators on this account thought less of him.
translations.idiomatic: His nature was impatient and quick to anger; commentators thought less of him for it.

sentences.zh: 子拯，伊闕令。

translations.literal: His son Zheng was magistrate of Yique.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zheng served as magistrate of Yique.

sentences.zh: 祿山之亂陷賊，不受偽命。

translations.literal: In the An Lushan rebellion he fell into rebel hands but did not accept false appointment.
translations.idiomatic: During the An Lushan rebellion he fell into rebel hands but refused to accept appointment under the rebel regime.

sentences.zh: 兩京克復，詔加太子右贊善。

translations.literal: When the two capitals were recovered, an edict added him as Right Supporter of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: After the two capitals were recovered he was appointed Right Supporter of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 弟九臯，自尚書郎歷唐、徐、宋、襄、廣五州刺史。

translations.literal: His younger brother Jiugao, from Director in the Secretariat, served in succession as prefect of Tang, Xu, Song, Xiang, and Guang.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Jiugao rose from a Secretariat director's post to serve in turn as prefect of Tang, Xu, Song, Xiang, and Guang prefectures.

sentences.zh: 九章，歷吉、明、曹三州刺史，鴻臚卿。

translations.literal: Jiuzhang served in succession as prefect of Ji, Ming, and Cao and as Director of the Court for Diplomatic Reception.
translations.idiomatic: Jiuzhang served in turn as prefect of Ji, Ming, and Cao prefectures and as Director of the Court for Diplomatic Reception.

sentences.zh: 九齡為中書令時，天長節百僚上壽，多獻珍異，唯九齡進《金鏡錄》五卷，言前古興廢之道，上賞異之。

translations.literal: When Jiuling was Director of the Secretariat, on the Tianzhang Festival the hundred officials offered longevity congratulations, most presenting rare treasures; only Jiuling presented five scrolls of the Golden Mirror Records, speaking of the ways of rise and fall in former antiquity; the Emperor admired this as exceptional.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiuling was Director of the Secretariat, on the Tianzhang Festival the officials offered birthday congratulations, most presenting rare treasures; Jiuling alone presented five scrolls of the Golden Mirror Records on the rise and fall of dynasties in antiquity, which the Emperor greatly admired.

sentences.zh: 又與中書侍郎嚴挺之、尚書左丞袁仁敬、右庶子梁升卿、御史中丞盧怡結交友善。

translations.literal: He also formed bonds of friendship with Vice Director of the Secretariat Yan Tingzhi, Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs Yuan Renjing, Right Subordinate Mentor Liang Shengqing, and Vice Censor-in-Chief Lu Yi.
translations.idiomatic: He also formed lasting friendships with Vice Director Yan Tingzhi, Left Vice Director Yuan Renjing, Right Subordinate Mentor Liang Shengqing, and Vice Censor-in-Chief Lu Yi.

sentences.zh: 挺之等有才幹，而交道終始不渝，甚為當時之所稱。

translations.literal: Tingzhi and the others had talent and capacity, yet their friendship from beginning to end never changed and was greatly praised by people of the time.
translations.idiomatic: Tingzhi and the others were men of talent, and their friendships with Jiuling never wavered from beginning to end—a quality much praised at the time.

sentences.zh: 至德初，上皇在蜀，思九齡之先覺，下詔褒贈，曰：「正大廈者柱石之力，昌帝業者輔相之臣。

translations.literal: Early in Zhide, the Retired Emperor was in Shu, thinking of Jiuling's prior foresight, and issued an edict of praise and posthumous grant, stating: "To set straight a great hall takes the strength of pillar and stone; to flourish an imperial enterprise takes the minister who assists.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhide era (756–758), the Retired Emperor in Shu recalled Jiuling's foresight and issued an edict of praise and posthumous honors: "To set straight a great hall requires pillar and stone; to flourish an imperial enterprise requires a assisting minister.

sentences.zh: 生則保其榮名，歿乃稱其盛德，節終未允於人望，加贈實存乎國章。

translations.literal: In life one preserves his honored name; in death one proclaims his great virtue—his life's end did not satisfy human expectation, and added posthumous grant truly resides in the state's regulations.
translations.idiomatic: In life one preserves honored name; in death one proclaims great virtue. His end did not satisfy the hopes of men, and an added posthumous grant truly belongs in the state's regulations.

sentences.zh: 故中書令張九齡，維嶽降神，濟川作相，開元之際，寅亮成功。

translations.literal: The late Director of the Secretariat Zhang Jiuling: the spirit descended from the sustaining mountain, he crossed the stream to serve as minister; in the Kaiyuan era he diligently assisted success.
translations.idiomatic: The late Director of the Secretariat Zhang Jiuling: spirit descended from the sustaining mountain, he crossed the stream to serve as minister; in the Kaiyuan era he diligently assisted the throne to success.

sentences.zh: 讜言定其社稷，先覺合於蓍策，永懷賢弼，可謂大臣。

translations.literal: His forthright words settled the altars of state; his prior foresight matched the yarrow stalks; eternally cherishing such a worthy assistant—he may be called a great minister.
translations.idiomatic: His forthright counsel secured the altars of state; his foresight matched the oracle stalks; to cherish such a worthy assistant forever is to know a great minister.

sentences.zh: 竹帛猶存，樵蘇必禁，爰從八命之秩，更進三臺之位。

translations.literal: Bamboo and silk still remain; fuel-gathering must be forbidden; from the rank of eight orders let him advance further to the position of the Three Terraces.
translations.idiomatic: His name endures on bamboo and silk; fuel-gathering at his tomb must be forbidden. From the rank of eight orders let him advance to the position of the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 可贈司徒，仍遣使就韶州致祭。」

translations.literal: He may be posthumously made Minister of Education, and an envoy is still sent to Shao Prefecture to perform sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: He is posthumously appointed Minister of Education, and an envoy is dispatched to Shaozhou to perform sacrifice."

sentences.zh: 有集二十卷。

translations.literal: He had a collected works in twenty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He left collected works in twenty scrolls.

sentences.zh: 張仲方九臯曾孫仲方，少朗秀。

translations.literal: Zhang Zhongfang, Jiugao's great-grandson Zhongfang, was bright and refined in youth.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhongfang, great-grandson of Jiugao, was bright and refined as a youth.

sentences.zh: 為兒童時，父友高郢見而奇之，曰；

translations.literal: When he was a child, his father's friend Gao Ying saw him and marveled, saying:
translations.idiomatic: As a child his father's friend Gao Ying saw him and marveled, saying,

sentences.zh: 「此子非常，必為國器，吾獲高位，必振發之。」

translations.literal: "This child is extraordinary and is sure to be a pillar of the state; if I gain high position, I am sure to raise him up.
translations.idiomatic: "This child is extraordinary and will surely be a pillar of the state. If I gain high office, I will surely raise him up."

sentences.zh: 後郢為御史大夫，首請仲方為御史。

translations.literal: Later when Ying was Censor-in-Chief, he first requested Zhongfang as censor.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Gao became Censor-in-Chief, he was the first to recommend Zhongfang as censor.

sentences.zh: 歷金州刺史。

translations.literal: He served as prefect of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: He served as prefect of Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 郡人有田產為中人所奪，仲方三疏奏聞，竟理其冤。

translations.literal: A man of the prefecture had his fields seized by a eunuch; Zhongfang memorialized three times to report it and in the end righted his wrong.
translations.idiomatic: A local man's fields were seized by a eunuch; Zhongfang memorialized three times and ultimately righted the injustice.

sentences.zh: 入為度支郎中，駁李吉甫謚，吉甫之黨惡之，出為遂州司馬。

translations.literal: He entered as Director in the Bureau of Revenue; he opposed Li Jifu's posthumous title; Jifu's faction hated him and he went out as Military Adjutant of Sui.
translations.idiomatic: He entered office as Director in the Bureau of Revenue and opposed Li Jifu's posthumous title; Jifu's faction hated him and he was sent out as military adjutant of Suizhou.

sentences.zh: 稍遷復、曹、鄭三郡守。

translations.literal: He was gradually transferred to serve as prefect of Fu, Cao, and Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: He was gradually promoted to serve as prefect of Fu, Cao, and Zheng.

sentences.zh: 為諫議大夫。

translations.literal: He became Remonstrance and Policy Advisor.
translations.idiomatic: He became Remonstrance and Policy Advisor.

sentences.zh: 時鄠縣令崔發因辱小黃門，敬宗赫怒，付臺推鞫。

translations.literal: At that time E Prefect Cui Fa, for insulting a junior yellow gate attendant, provoked Jingzong's fierce anger; he was handed to the censorate for investigation.
translations.idiomatic: E Prefect Cui Fa insulted a junior eunuch attendant, provoking Emperor Jingzong's fierce anger; he was handed over to the censorate for investigation.

sentences.zh: 及元日大赦，獨發不得宥。

translations.literal: When the New Year's Day general amnesty came, Fa alone was not pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: When the New Year's general amnesty was proclaimed, Cui Fa alone was excluded.

sentences.zh: 仲方上疏，其略曰：「鴻恩將布於天下，而不行御前；

translations.literal: Zhongfang submitted a memorial, its gist stating: "The great grace is about to be spread over all under Heaven, yet it does not reach before the throne;
translations.idiomatic: Zhongfang memorialized in essence: "The great grace is about to spread over the empire, yet it does not reach before the throne;

sentences.zh: 霈澤始被於昆蟲，而獨遺崔發。」

translations.literal: the generous rain is first bestowed on insects, yet Cui Fa alone is left out.
translations.idiomatic: the generous rain first reaches even insects, yet Cui Fa alone is left out."

sentences.zh: 由是發得不死，時論美之。

translations.literal: On this account Fa did not die, and opinion of the time praised this.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Fa was spared death as a result, and contemporaries praised Zhongfang.

sentences.zh: 大和九年，為京兆尹，將相從累者皆大戮，仲方密令識之。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Dahe he was Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao; those of minister and general rank who followed in succession were all greatly slaughtered, and Zhongfang secretly ordered them identified.
translations.idiomatic: In 835, as Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao, when ministers and generals connected to the Sweet Dew incident were slaughtered en masse, Zhongfang secretly ordered their bodies identified.

sentences.zh: 旋詔下許令收葬，得認遺骸，實仲方之力也。

translations.literal: Soon an edict was issued permitting burial; the remains could be identified—this was truly Zhongfang's achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Before long an imperial edict allowed the dead to be gathered for burial, and the remains could be identified—an outcome owed entirely to Zhongfang's efforts.

sentences.zh: 是時軍人橫恣，仲方脂韋，坐不稱職，出為華州刺史，改秘書監。

translations.literal: At that time soldiers were overbearing and unrestrained; Zhongfang was soft and timid, judged unfit for his post, sent out as governor of Hua Prefecture, and then made Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers were running rampant at the time, and Zhongfang was regarded as too mild and ineffectual for the crisis. He was found unfit for office, appointed governor of Hua Prefecture, and later transferred to be Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 開成二年卒，年七十二，贈禮部尚書，謚曰成。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaicheng he died, aged seventy-two; posthumously made Minister of Rites, posthumous title Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of the Kaicheng era, at the age of seventy-two. He was posthumously appointed Minister of Rites and given the posthumous name Cheng.

sentences.zh: 李適之，一名昌，恆山王承乾之孫也。

translations.literal: Li Shizhi—Li Shizhi, also named Chang, was a grandson of Prince of Hengshan Chengqian.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shizhi, also known as Chang, was a grandson of the Prince of Hengshan, Li Chengqian.

sentences.zh: 父象，官至懷州別駕。

translations.literal: His father Xiang reached the office of Biejia of Huaizhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father, Xiang, rose to the post of vice-prefect of Huaizhou.

sentences.zh: 適之神龍初起家拜左衛郎將。

translations.literal: Shizhi first entered service at the beginning of Shenlong, appointed Left Guard Langjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhi began his career at the start of the Shenlong era, when he was appointed a captain in the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 開元中，累遷通州刺史，以強幹見稱。

translations.literal: In the Kaiyuan period he was repeatedly promoted to governor of Tong Prefecture and was renowned for forceful competence.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaiyuan reign he rose through several posts to become governor of Tong Prefecture, where he earned a reputation for vigorous and capable administration.

sentences.zh: 時給事中韓朝宗為按察使，特表薦之，擢拜秦州都督。

translations.literal: At that time Jishizhong Han Chaozong served as inspection commissioner; he specially memorialized to recommend him, and he was promoted and appointed Area Commander of Qin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Chaozong of the Secretariat was serving as an inspection commissioner, he singled Shizhi out in a memorial of recommendation, and Shizhi was promoted to Area Commander of Qin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 俄轉陜州刺史，入為河南尹。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to governor of Shan Prefecture, then entered the capital as Henan Intendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to governor of Shan Prefecture and then recalled to the capital as Intendant of Henan.

sentences.zh: 適之性簡率，不務苛細，人吏便之。

translations.literal: Shizhi's nature was plain and direct; he did not pursue petty exactness, and officials and clerks found him convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhi was straightforward by nature and did not fuss over petty detail, which made life easier for his staff and subordinates.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，拜御史大夫。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was appointed Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: A little over a year later he was appointed Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 開元二十七年，兼幽州大都督府長史，知節度事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year of Kaiyuan he concurrently served as chief administrator of the Youzhou Area Command, managing military commission affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year of Kaiyuan he also served as chief administrator of the Youzhou metropolitan commandery and oversaw the military commission there.

sentences.zh: 適之以祖得罪見廢，父又遭則天所黜，葬禮有闕，上疏請歸葬昭陵之闕內。

translations.literal: Because Shizhi's grandfather had been condemned and deposed, and his father had also been demoted by Empress Wu, the funeral rites had been deficient; he submitted a memorial requesting reburial within the gap at Zhaoling.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhi's grandfather had been condemned and stripped of rank, and his father had later been demoted by Empress Wu, leaving the family funerals incomplete. He submitted a memorial asking that the remains be reinterred in the vacant place at Zhaoling.

sentences.zh: 於是下詔追贈承乾為恆山湣王，象為越州都督、郇國公，伯父厥及亡兄數人並有褒贈。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict was issued posthumously enfeoffing Chengqian as Prince Min of Hengshan, Xiang as Area Commander of Yue Prefecture and Duke of Xun, and several paternal uncles and deceased elder brothers all received commendatory posthumous honors.
translations.idiomatic: The throne then issued an edict posthumously restoring Chengqian as Prince Min of Hengshan and honoring Xiang as Area Commander of Yue and Duke of Xun, while several uncles and deceased elder brothers received posthumous awards as well.

sentences.zh: 數喪同至京師，葬禮甚盛，仍刊石於墳所。

translations.literal: Several coffins arrived together in the capital; the funeral was very grand, and stone was still carved at the grave site.
translations.idiomatic: Several coffins were brought to the capital together, the funeral was conducted on a grand scale, and commemorative stones were carved at the burial site.

sentences.zh: 俄拜刑部尚書。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 適之雅好賓友，飲酒一斗不亂，夜則宴賞，晝決公務，庭無留事。

translations.literal: Shizhi greatly loved guests and friends; he could drink a dou of wine without disorder. At night he feasted and enjoyed himself; by day he decided public affairs, and nothing was left pending in the court.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhi was fond of entertaining friends and could drink a gallon of wine without losing his composure. He held banquets at night and cleared official business by day, so that nothing lingered on his desk.

sentences.zh: 天寶元年，代牛仙客為左相，累封清和縣公。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianbao he replaced Niu Xianke as Left Chancellor and was repeatedly enfeoffed as Duke of Qinghe County.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianbao he succeeded Niu Xianke as Left Chancellor and was enfeoffed in succession as Duke of Qinghe County.

sentences.zh: 與李林甫爭權不葉，適之性疏，為其陰中。

translations.literal: He struggled with Li Linfu for power without harmony; Shizhi's nature was open and careless, and Linfu struck at him in secret.
translations.idiomatic: He clashed with Li Linfu over power, and because Shizhi was open and unsuspecting, Linfu undermined him from the shadows.

sentences.zh: 林甫嘗謂適之曰：「華山有金鑛，采之可以富國，上未之知。」

translations.literal: Linfu once said to Shizhi: "Mount Hua has gold ore; mining it could enrich the state—the Emperor does not yet know this.
translations.idiomatic: Linfu once told Shizhi, "Mount Hua holds gold ore. Mining it could enrich the empire, but His Majesty does not yet know of it."

sentences.zh: 適之心善其言，他日從容奏之。

translations.literal: Shizhi took his words to heart and on another day calmly reported them to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhi was pleased by the suggestion and, on a later occasion, mentioned it to the emperor in an easy, informal manner.

sentences.zh: 玄宗大悅，顧問林甫，對曰：「臣知之久矣。

translations.literal: Xuanzong was greatly pleased and turned to ask Linfu; he replied: "Your servant has known of this for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong was delighted and turned to Li Linfu for confirmation. Linfu answered, "I have known of this for a long time.

sentences.zh: 然華山陛下本命，王氣所在，不可穿鑿，臣故不敢上言。」

translations.literal: Yet Mount Hua is Your Majesty's natal mountain, where royal qi resides; it must not be bored and dug into—your servant therefore dared not speak of it.
translations.idiomatic: But Mount Hua is Your Majesty's natal mountain, the seat of the dynasty's vital force. It must not be mined, and that is why I did not dare bring it up."

sentences.zh: 帝以為愛己，薄適之言疏。

translations.literal: The Emperor thought this showed love for himself and regarded Shizhi's words as careless and shallow.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took this as proof of Linfu's devotion to him and began to look on Shizhi's counsel as careless and ill-considered.

sentences.zh: 隴右節度皇甫惟明、刑部尚書韋堅、戶部尚書裴寬、京兆尹韓朝宗，悉與適之善，林甫皆中傷之，構成其罪，相繼放逐。

translations.literal: Longyou Military Commissioner Huangfu Weiming, Minister of Justice Wei Jian, Minister of Revenue Pei Kuan, and Jingzhao Intendant Han Chaozong were all on good terms with Shizhi; Linfu slandered them all, fabricated their crimes, and they were banished one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Weiming, military commissioner of Longyou; Wei Jian, Minister of Justice; Pei Kuan, Minister of Revenue; and Han Chaozong, Intendant of Jingzhao—all were close to Shizhi. Li Linfu slandered each of them, fabricated charges, and they were exiled in succession.

sentences.zh: 適之懼不自安，求為散職。

translations.literal: Shizhi, fearful and ill at ease, requested an honorary post without duties.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing for his safety, Shizhi asked to be given a honorific post without real responsibility.

sentences.zh: 五載，罷知政事，守太子少保。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was removed from handling state affairs and kept the post of Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Tianbao he was dismissed from the chancellorship and retained only the title of Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 遽命親故歡會，賦詩曰：「避賢初罷相，樂聖且銜杯。

translations.literal: He promptly ordered relatives and friends to a merry gathering and composed a poem saying: "Having yielded the post of chancellor to worthier men, I now delight in the sage and raise my cup.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately summoned relatives and friends to a celebration and wrote a poem that began, "Having stepped aside from the chancellorship, I now take joy in wine and lift my cup.

sentences.zh: 為問門前客，今朝幾個來？」

translations.literal: I ask the guests at my gate: how many have come today?
translations.idiomatic: Tell me, guests at my gate—how many of you came today?"

sentences.zh: 竟坐與韋堅等相善，貶宜春太守。

translations.literal: In the end, because he was friendly with Wei Jian and others, he was demoted to prefect of Yichun.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he was demoted to prefect of Yichun on the charge of his association with Wei Jian and the others.

sentences.zh: 後御史羅希奭奉使殺韋堅、盧幼臨、裴敦復、李邕等於貶所，州縣且聞希奭到，無不惶駭。

translations.literal: Later Censor Luo Xiyi was sent on mission to kill Wei Jian, Lu Youlin, Pei Dunfu, Li Yong, and others at their places of exile; whenever prefectures and counties heard that Xiyi was arriving, none failed to be struck with terror.
translations.idiomatic: Later the censor Luo Xiyi was dispatched to execute Wei Jian, Lu Youlin, Pei Dunfu, Li Yong, and others in exile. Wherever word spread that Xiyi was coming, officials and commoners alike were seized with dread.

sentences.zh: 希奭過宜春郡，適之聞其來，仰藥而死。

translations.literal: When Xiyi passed through Yichun Prefecture, Shizhi heard of his coming and took poison, dying.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiyi passed through Yichun, Shizhi learned that he was on his way and swallowed poison to die.

sentences.zh: 李季卿子季卿，弱冠舉明經，頗工文詞。

translations.literal: Li Jiqing—Zi Jiqing—at the age of weak cap passed the Mingjing examination and was quite skilled in literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jiqing, styled Zi Jiqing, passed the Mingjing examination in his youth and showed considerable talent for literary composition.

sentences.zh: 應制舉，登博學宏詞科，再遷京兆府鄠縣尉。

translations.literal: He answered a special imperial examination, passed the Broad Learning and Grand Rhetoric subject, and was twice promoted to Wei of Hu County in the Jingzhao prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He took the special imperial examination and passed in Broad Learning and Eloquent Composition, then rose twice to the post of county magistrate of Hu in the Jingzhao metropolitan prefecture.

sentences.zh: 肅宗朝，累遷中書舍人，以公事坐貶通州別駕。

translations.literal: In the Suzong reign he was repeatedly promoted to Secretariat Drafter; because of an official matter he was demoted to Biejia of Tong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Suzong he rose through several posts to Secretariat Drafter, but was later demoted to vice-prefect of Tong Prefecture on an official charge.

sentences.zh: 代宗即位，大舉淹抑，自通州徵為京兆少尹。

translations.literal: When Daizong took the throne, he broadly raised those long held back; Jiqing was summoned from Tong Prefecture to be Junior Intendant of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Daizong came to the throne, he launched a broad effort to recall men who had long been passed over, and Jiqing was summoned from Tong Prefecture to serve as Junior Intendant of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 尋復中書舍人，拜吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: Soon he was again made Secretariat Drafter and appointed Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon restored as Secretariat Drafter and then appointed Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 俄兼御史大夫，奉使河南、江淮宣慰，振拔幽滯，進用忠廉，時人稱之。

translations.literal: Soon he concurrently served as Censor-in-Chief and was sent on mission to console Henan and the Jiang-Huai region; he raised the obscure and long-stagnant and advanced the loyal and incorrupt, and people of the time praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was also made Censor-in-Chief and sent on a consolation mission through Henan and the Jiang-Huai region, where he promoted neglected talent and advanced loyal, upright men—conduct for which contemporaries praised him.

sentences.zh: 在銓衡數年，轉右散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He spent several years in charge of selection and was transferred to Right Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: After several years overseeing personnel selection, he was transferred to Right Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 季卿有宇量，性識博達，善與人交，襟懷豁如。

translations.literal: Jiqing had breadth of bearing, a nature and understanding broad and penetrating, skill in dealing with people, and a mind open and spacious.
translations.idiomatic: Jiqing had a generous spirit and wide-ranging knowledge, was skilled at friendship, and carried himself with an open and easy manner.

sentences.zh: 其在朝以進賢為務，士以此多之。

translations.literal: In court he made advancing the worthy his task, and scholars for this reason esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: At court he made the promotion of worthy men his chief concern, and for this the scholarly class held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 大曆二年卒，贈禮部尚書。

translations.literal: In the second year of Dali he died; posthumously made Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of the Dali era and was posthumously appointed Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 李融孫融，立性嚴整，善吏事。

translations.literal: Li Rong—Sun Rong—had a nature upright and strict and was skilled in administrative affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Li Rong, styled Sun Rong, was upright and disciplined by nature and skilled in administrative affairs.

sentences.zh: 貞元十年，歷官至渭州節度使卒。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Zhenyuan, having risen through offices, he died as Military Commissioner of Wei Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Zhenyuan he died in office as military commissioner of Wei Prefecture, having risen through a series of posts.

sentences.zh: 嚴挺之，華州華陰人。

translations.literal: Yan Tingzhi—Yan Tingzhi—was a native of Huayin in Hua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Tingzhi was a native of Huayin in Hua Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 叔父方嶷，景雲中戶部郎中。

translations.literal: His uncle Fangyan, in the Jingyun period, was Langzhong in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Fangyan served as a director in the Ministry of Revenue during the Jingyun era.

sentences.zh: 挺之少好學，舉進士。

translations.literal: Tingzhi in youth loved learning and passed the Jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Tingzhi was studious from youth and passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 神龍元年，制舉擢第，授義興尉。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shenlong he was selected in a special imperial examination and appointed Wei of Yixing.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shenlong he passed a special imperial examination and was appointed magistrate of Yixing.

sentences.zh: 遇姚崇為常州刺史，見其體質昂藏，雅有吏幹，深器異之。

translations.literal: He encountered Yao Chong serving as governor of Chang Prefecture; seeing his physique lofty and imposing and his elegant administrative ability, Chong greatly valued and regarded him as extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: When Yao Chong was governor of Chang Prefecture, he noticed Tingzhi's imposing bearing and natural talent for administration and came to think very highly of him.

sentences.zh: 及崇再入為中書令，引挺之為右拾遺。

translations.literal: When Chong again entered office as Zhongshu Ling, he brought in Tingzhi as Right Reminder.
translations.idiomatic: When Chong returned to power as Director of the Secretariat, he brought Tingzhi in as a Right Reminder.

sentences.zh: 睿宗好樂，聽之忘倦，玄宗又善音律。

translations.literal: Ruizong loved music and listened until he forgot weariness; Xuanzong was also skilled in musical theory.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ruizong loved music and would listen until he forgot his fatigue, and Emperor Xuanzong was also accomplished in musical theory.

sentences.zh: 先天二年正月望，胡僧婆陀請夜開門燃百千燈，睿宗禦延喜門觀樂，凡經四日。

translations.literal: On the full moon of the first month of the second year of Xiantian, the foreign monk Botuo requested that the gates be opened at night and a hundred thousand lamps lit; Ruizong attended at Yanxi Gate to watch the music, altogether for four days.
translations.idiomatic: On the first full moon of the second year of Xiantian, the foreign monk Botuo asked that the city gates be opened at night and a hundred thousand lamps lit. Ruizong watched the performances from Yanxi Gate for four days in all.

sentences.zh: 又追作先天元年大酺，睿宗禦安福門樓觀百司酺宴，以夜繼晝，經月餘日。

translations.literal: They also re-enacted the great communal feast of the first year of Xiantian; Ruizong attended the Anfu Gate tower to watch the hundred offices' feast banquet, night following day, for more than a month.
translations.idiomatic: They also staged again the grand communal feast of the first year of Xiantian. Ruizong watched from the tower of Anfu Gate as the ministries held their banquets, night after day, for more than a month.

sentences.zh: 挺之上疏諫曰：微臣竊惟陛下應天順人，發號施令，躬親大禮，昭布鴻澤，孜孜庶政，業業萬幾。蓋以天下心為心，深戒安危之理，此誠堯、舜、禹、湯之德教也。奈何親禦城門，以觀大酺，累日兼夜，臣愚竊所未諭。夫酺者，因人所利，合醵為歡，無相奪倫，不至糜弊。且臣卜其晝，史冊攸存，君舉必書，帝王重慎。今乃暴衣冠於上路，羅妓樂於中宵。雜鄭、衛之音，縱倡優之樂。陛下還淳復古，宵衣旰食，不矜細行，恐非聖德所宜。臣以為一不可也。誰何警夜，伐鼓通晨，以備非常，存之善教。今陛下不深惟戒慎，輕違動息，重門弛禁，巨猾多徒。倘有躍馬奔車，流言駭叫，一塵聽覽，有累宸衷。臣以為二不可也。且一人向隅，滿堂不樂；一物失所，納隍增慮。陛下北宮多暇，西墉暫臨。青春日長，已積埃塵之弊；紫微漏永，重窮歌舞之樂。倘令有司跛倚，下人饑倦，以陛下近猶不恤，而況於遠乎！聖情攸聞，豈不懍然只畏。臣以為三不可也。且元正首祚，大禮頻光，百姓颙颙，咸謂業盛配天，功垂曠代。今陛下恩似薄於眾望，酺即過於往年。王公貴人，各承微旨；州縣坊曲，競為課稅。籲嗟道路，貿易家產，損萬人之力，營百戲之資。適欲同其歡，而乃遺其患，復令兼夜，人何以堪？臣以為四不可也。《書》曰：「罔咈百姓，以從己之欲。」況自去夏霪霖，經今亢旱，農乏收成，市有騰貴。損其實，崇其虛，馳不急之務，擾方春之業。前代聖主明王，忽於細微而成過患多矣，陛下可效之哉？伏望晝則歡娛，暮令休息，要令兼夜，恐無益於聖朝。

translations.literal: Tingzhi submitted a memorial of remonstrance, saying: Your lowly subject privately considers that Your Majesty responds to Heaven and accords with the people, issues commands and orders, personally performs the great rites, brightly spreads vast grace, diligently attends to the various policies, and reverently handles the myriad affairs. This is because you take the heart of the realm as your own heart and deeply guard against the principles of security and danger. This is truly the virtuous teaching of Yao, Shun, Yu, and Tang. How is it, then, that you personally come to the city gate to watch the great communal feast, continuing through many days and nights? Your foolish subject privately does not understand it. As for a communal feast, it follows what benefits the people, combines contributions to make joy, does not cause people to seize one another's proper order, and does not reach waste and ruin. Moreover, your subject would choose daylight for it. The point is preserved in the historical records: the ruler's actions must be written down, and emperors and kings treat them with great care. Now officials in formal caps and robes are exposed on the upper road, and entertainers and music are arrayed in the middle of the night. The sounds of Zheng and Wei are mixed in, and the amusements of actors and performers are indulged. Your Majesty returns to simplicity and restores antiquity, dressing before dawn and eating late; if you do not take care over small conduct, I fear it is not what sacred virtue should do. Your subject considers this the first reason it must not be done. Challenging and questioning at night and beating drums until morning are used to guard against emergencies, and preserving them is good instruction. Now Your Majesty does not deeply think on caution and care, lightly violates the pattern of movement and rest, relaxes the prohibitions of the layered gates, and great villains have many followers. If there were leaping horses and rushing carriages, or rumors and alarming cries, even one speck reaching your hearing and sight would burden the imperial heart. Your subject considers this the second reason it must not be done. Moreover, if one person faces the corner, the whole hall is not joyful; if one thing loses its place, the anxiety of seeing people fallen into a ditch is increased. Your Majesty has much leisure in the northern palace and briefly visits the western wall. The days of spring youth are long, and already the harm of dust has accumulated; the watches of Ziwei are lengthy, and you again exhaust the pleasures of song and dance. If this makes the responsible officials lean and limp, and those below hungry and weary, and Your Majesty does not show concern even for those nearby, how much less for those far away? When the sacred feelings hear of it, how could they not be solemnly fearful? Your subject considers this the third reason it must not be done. Moreover, at the first blessing of the first day of the year, the great rites have repeatedly shone; the common people look upward and all say that the enterprise flourishes enough to match Heaven and that the achievement will hang over distant ages. Now Your Majesty's grace seems thin compared with the hopes of the masses, while the feast surpasses past years. Princes, dukes, and nobles each receive subtle instructions; prefectures, counties, wards, and lanes compete to levy assessments. Sighing fills the roads as people trade away their family property, diminishing the strength of ten thousand people to provide the resources for a hundred entertainments. You wished only to share their joy, but instead leave them with harm; if you again order it to continue through the night, how can the people bear it? Your subject considers this the fourth reason it must not be done. The Documents says, "Do not go against the hundred surnames in order to follow your own desires." Moreover, since last summer there have been soaking rains, and now there has been drought; farmers lack harvests, and prices in the markets have risen. To diminish what is real and exalt what is empty, to rush after tasks that are not urgent and disturb the work of spring: in former generations, many sage rulers and enlightened kings created faults and disasters by neglecting small matters. Can Your Majesty imitate them? I humbly hope that by day there may be rejoicing and entertainment, but at dusk people will be ordered to rest. If you must order it to continue through the night, I fear it will bring no benefit to the sacred court.

sentences.zh: 上納其言而止。

translations.literal: The Emperor accepted his words and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted his advice and put a stop to the festivities.

sentences.zh: 時侍御史任知古恃憲威，於朝行詬詈衣冠，挺之深讓之，以為不敬，乃為臺司所劾，左遷萬州員外參軍。

translations.literal: At that time Attending Censor Ren Zhigu relied on the censorate's authority and in the court procession reviled officials in formal dress; Tingzhi sternly reproached him as disrespectful, and for this the censorate office impeached him and he was demoted to Outside Staff Member of Wan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the attending censor Ren Zhigu abused the authority of the censorate and hurled insults at court officials in procession. Tingzhi sharply rebuked him for disrespect, but the censorate in turn impeached Tingzhi, and he was demoted to an outside staff post in Wan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 開元中，為考功員外郎。

translations.literal: In the Kaiyuan period he served as Outside Director in the Bureau of Evaluations.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaiyuan reign he served as an outside director in the Bureau of Evaluations.

sentences.zh: 典舉二年，大稱平允，登科者頓減二分之一。

translations.literal: He presided over examinations for two years and was greatly praised for fairness; those who passed the examinations were suddenly reduced by one half.
translations.idiomatic: He oversaw the examinations for two years and won wide praise for fairness, cutting the number who passed by half.

sentences.zh: 遷考功郎中，特敕又令知考功貢舉事，稍遷給事中。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Langzhong in the Bureau of Evaluations; by special edict he was again ordered to oversee evaluation and tribute-examination affairs, and was gradually promoted to Jishizhong.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to director in the Bureau of Evaluations and, by special edict, was again put in charge of the civil examinations. He was later promoted step by step to Secretariat Drafter.

sentences.zh: 時黃門侍郎杜暹、中書侍郎李元纮同列為相，不葉。

translations.literal: At that time Huangmen Shilang Du Xian and Zhongshu Shilang Li Yuanhong served together as chancellors and were not in harmony.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Du Xian, Vice Director of the Chancellery, and Li Yuanhong, Vice Director of the Secretariat, served together as chancellors and did not get along.

sentences.zh: 暹與挺之善，元纮素重宋遙，引為中書舍人。

translations.literal: Xian was on good terms with Tingzhi; Yuanhong had long esteemed Song Yao and brought him in as Zhongshu Sheren.
translations.idiomatic: Du Xian was friendly with Tingzhi, while Yuanhong had long favored Song Yao and brought him in as a Secretariat drafter.

sentences.zh: 及與起居舍人張咺等同考吏部等第判，遙復與挺之好尚不同，遙言於元纮。

translations.literal: When together with Qiju Sheren Zhang Xuan and others they examined and graded the Ministry of Personnel lists, Yao again differed from Tingzhi in preferences and standards; Yao spoke of this to Yuanhong.
translations.idiomatic: When he joined with the diarist Zhang Xuan and others to grade the Ministry of Personnel lists, Yao again clashed with Tingzhi over standards and reported the disagreement to Yuanhong.

sentences.zh: 元纮詰譙挺之，挺之曰：「明公位尊國相，情溺小人，乃有憎惡，甚為不取也。」

translations.literal: Yuanhong interrogated and reproached Tingzhi; Tingzhi said: "Your Excellency holds the honored post of state chancellor, yet your feelings dote on petty men and you harbor dislike—this is very unbecoming.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanhong challenged and rebuked Tingzhi. Tingzhi replied, "Your Excellency holds the highest office in the land, yet you indulge petty men and harbor personal grudges—that is hardly fitting for a chief minister."

sentences.zh: 詞色俱厲。

translations.literal: Both words and expression were severe.
translations.idiomatic: His words and manner were both fierce.

sentences.zh: 元纮曰：「小人為誰？」

translations.literal: Yuanhong said: "Who is the petty man?
translations.idiomatic: Yuanhong asked, "Who is this petty man?"

sentences.zh: 挺之曰：「即宋遙也。」

translations.literal: Tingzhi said: "It is Song Yao."
translations.idiomatic: Tingzhi answered, "Song Yao."

sentences.zh: 因出為登州刺史、太原少尹。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was sent out as governor of Deng Prefecture and Junior Intendant of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: For this he was sent out to serve as governor of Deng Prefecture and then Junior Intendant of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 殿中監王毛仲使太原、朔方、幽州，計會兵馬，事隔數年，乃牒太原索器仗。

translations.literal: Director of the Palace Domestic Service Wang Maoqi had been sent to Taiyuan, Shuofang, and You Prefectures to tally troops and horses; the matter had been separated by several years, and he then sent a dispatch to Taiyuan demanding arms and equipment.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Maoqi of the Palace Domestic Service had been sent to Taiyuan, Shuofang, and You to audit troops and horses. Years passed, and he then sent an official dispatch to Taiyuan demanding arms and equipment.

sentences.zh: 挺之以不挾敕，毛仲寵幸久，恐有變故，密奏之。

translations.literal: Tingzhi, because he carried no imperial edict, and because Maoqi had long enjoyed favor and privilege, feared there might be trouble and secretly memorialized about it.
translations.idiomatic: Tingzhi noted that Maoqi carried no imperial commission. Maoqi had long enjoyed the emperor's favor, and Tingzhi feared trouble might follow, so he reported the matter in a secret memorial.

sentences.zh: 尋遷濮、汴二州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to be governor of Pu and Bian Prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to serve as governor of Pu and then Bian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 挺之所歷皆嚴整，吏不敢犯，及蒞大郡，人乃重足側息。

translations.literal: Every place Tingzhi governed was strict and orderly; clerks did not dare offend, and when he arrived at great prefectures people would stand with feet together and hold their breath.
translations.idiomatic: Every post Tingzhi held was run with strict discipline, and subordinates did not dare transgress. When he took charge of a major prefecture, people walked in fear and scarcely dared breathe aloud.

sentences.zh: 二十年，毛仲得罪賜死，玄宗思曩日之奏，擢為刑部侍郎，深見恩遇，改太府卿。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year Maoqi offended and was ordered to die; Xuanzong recalled his memorial of former days, promoted him to Vice Minister of Justice, deeply favored him, and changed his post to Director of the Grand Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year Wang Maoqi fell from favor and was ordered to die. Xuanzong remembered Tingzhi's earlier memorial, promoted him to Vice Minister of Justice, and showed him deep favor before appointing him Director of the Grand Treasury.

sentences.zh: 與張九齡相善，九齡入相，用挺之為尚書左丞，知吏部選，陸景融知兵部選，皆為一時精選。

translations.literal: He was on good terms with Zhang Jiuling; when Jiuling entered the chancellorship he used Tingzhi as Left Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs, overseeing Ministry of Personnel selection, and Lu Jingrong oversaw Ministry of War selection—both were fine choices of the time.
translations.idiomatic: He was close to Zhang Jiuling. When Jiuling became chancellor, he appointed Tingzhi Left Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs to oversee personnel selection, with Lu Jingrong overseeing military appointments—both were regarded as outstanding appointments of the day.

sentences.zh: 時侍中裴耀卿、禮部尚書李林甫與九齡同在相位，九齡以詞學進，入視草翰林，又為中書令，甚承恩顧。

translations.literal: At that time Shizhong Pei Yaojing, Minister of Rites Li Linfu, and Jiuling all held chancellorship together; Jiuling had advanced through literary learning, entered to review drafts in the Hanlin, and was also Zhongshu Ling, greatly receiving imperial favor.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Pei Yaojing as Palace Attendant, Li Linfu as Minister of Rites, and Zhang Jiuling all served together as chancellors. Jiuling had risen through literary talent, reviewed drafts in the Hanlin Academy, and also served as Director of the Secretariat, enjoying exceptional favor from the throne.

sentences.zh: 耀卿與九齡素善，林甫巧密，知九齡方承恩遇，善事之，意未相與。

translations.literal: Yaojing and Jiuling had long been friendly; Linfu was crafty and subtle, knew Jiuling was then receiving favor, treated him well, but in mind was not truly allied with him.
translations.idiomatic: Yaojing and Jiuling had long been on good terms. Linfu was subtle and calculating; seeing that Jiuling was in favor, he treated him well outwardly, but in his heart he was no ally.

sentences.zh: 林甫引蕭炅為戶部侍郎，嘗與挺之同行慶吊，客次有《禮記》，蕭炅讀之曰：「蒸嘗伏獵。」

translations.literal: Linfu brought in Xiao Jiong as Vice Minister of Revenue; he once traveled with Tingzhi on a condolence or congratulation visit, and at a guest stop there was the Book of Rites; Xiao Jiong read it saying: "The seasonal offerings—prostrate hunting.
translations.idiomatic: Li Linfu had brought Xiao Jiong in as Vice Minister of Revenue. Once, on a condolence visit with Tingzhi, Xiao Jiong picked up a copy of the Book of Rites at an inn and read aloud, "The seasonal offerings—prostrate hunting."

sentences.zh: 炅早從官，無學術，不識「伏臘」之意，誤讀之。

translations.literal: Jiong had entered office early, had no learning, did not know the meaning of "wax and harvest festivals," and misread it.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong had entered office young and had little learning. He did not know the meaning of "fula", the wax and harvest festivals, and misread the characters.

sentences.zh: 挺之戲問，炅對如初。

translations.literal: Tingzhi jokingly questioned him; Jiong answered as at first.
translations.idiomatic: Tingzhi questioned him in jest, and Jiong repeated the same mistake.

sentences.zh: 挺之白九齡曰：「省中豈有『伏獵侍郎。』」

translations.literal: Tingzhi told Jiuling: "How can there be in the Secretariat a 'Prostrate Hunting Vice Minister'?
translations.idiomatic: Tingzhi told Zhang Jiuling, "Can the Secretariat really harbor a 'Prostrate Hunting Vice Minister'?"

sentences.zh: 由是出為岐州刺史，林甫深恨之。

translations.literal: For this he was sent out as governor of Qi Prefecture, and Linfu deeply resented him.
translations.idiomatic: For this remark Xiao Jiong was sent out as governor of Qi Prefecture, and Li Linfu came to hate Tingzhi deeply.

sentences.zh: 九齡嘗欲引挺之同居相位，謂之曰：「李尚書深承聖恩，足下宜一造門款狎。」

translations.literal: Jiuling once wished to bring Tingzhi to share the chancellorship with him and said to him: "Vice Minister Li deeply enjoys the sage's grace; you ought to pay one visit to his gate and become familiar and intimate.
translations.idiomatic: Jiuling once wanted to bring Tingzhi into the chancellorship with him and said, "Minister Li enjoys deep favor from His Majesty. You ought to call on him at least once and cultivate a cordial acquaintance."

sentences.zh: 挺之素負氣，薄其為人，三年，非公事竟不私造其門，以此彌為林甫所嫉。

translations.literal: Tingzhi had long been proud by nature and looked down on his character; for three years, apart from public business, he never privately visited his gate, and for this Linfu resented him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Tingzhi had always been proud by nature and despised Linfu's character. For three years he never paid a private visit to Linfu's house except on official business, and this only deepened Linfu's resentment.

sentences.zh: 及挺之囑蔚州刺史王元琰，林甫使人詰於禁中，以此九齡罷相，挺之出為洺州刺史，二十九年，移絳郡太守。

translations.literal: When Tingzhi interceded for Wang Yuanyan, governor of Yu Prefecture, Linfu sent men to interrogate him within the palace precinct; for this Jiuling was removed from the chancellorship, Tingzhi was sent out as governor of Ming Prefecture, and in the twenty-ninth year was moved to prefect of Jiang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Tingzhi interceded for Wang Yuanyan, prefect of Yu, Li Linfu had him questioned inside the palace. Zhang Jiuling was dismissed from the chancellorship as a result, and Tingzhi was sent out as governor of Ming Prefecture. In the twenty-ninth year he was transferred to be prefect of Jiang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 天寶元年，玄宗嘗謂林甫曰：「嚴挺之何在？

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianbao Xuanzong once said to Linfu: "Where is Yan Tingzhi?
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianbao, Xuanzong once asked Li Linfu, "Where is Yan Tingzhi?

sentences.zh: 此人亦堪進用。」

translations.literal: This man is also fit to be advanced and employed.
translations.idiomatic: He is still a man worth promoting."

sentences.zh: 林甫乃召其弟損之至門敘故，云「當授子員外郎」，因謂之曰：「聖人視賢兄極深，要須作一計，入城對見，當有大用。」

translations.literal: Linfu then summoned his younger brother Sunzhi to his gate to speak of old ties, saying "Your son will be appointed Outside Lang," and then said to him: "The Sage views your worthy elder brother with the deepest regard; you must devise a plan—enter the city for an audience, and there will be great employment."
translations.idiomatic: Li Linfu then summoned Tingzhi's younger brother Sunzhi to his house to renew old acquaintance, promising that Sunzhi's son would be given an outside post. He told Sunzhi, "His Majesty thinks very highly of your elder brother. You must find a way for him to enter the capital for an audience—he will surely be given a major appointment."

sentences.zh: 令損之取絳郡一狀，云：「有少風氣，請入京就醫。」

translations.literal: He ordered Sunzhi to obtain a petition from Jiang Commandery saying: "He has a slight wind ailment and requests to enter the capital for medical treatment."
translations.idiomatic: He had Sunzhi obtain a petition from Jiang Commandery stating, "He has a mild wind disorder and asks permission to enter the capital for treatment."

sentences.zh: 林甫將狀奏云：「挺之年高，近患風，且須授閑官就醫。」

translations.literal: Linfu was about to memorialize the petition saying: "Tingzhi is advanced in years and recently afflicted with wind; he should be given an honorary post and allowed to seek medical treatment."
translations.idiomatic: Li Linfu then submitted the petition with the comment, "Tingzhi is elderly and has recently suffered from wind disorder. He should be given an honorary post and allowed to seek treatment."

sentences.zh: 玄宗嘆叱久之。

translations.literal: Xuanzong sighed and reproached for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong sighed and muttered his displeasure for a long while.

sentences.zh: 林甫奏授員外詹事，便令東京養疾。

translations.literal: Linfu memorialized to appoint him Outside Household Tutor and immediately ordered him to convalesce in the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Li Linfu then memorialized to appoint Tingzhi an outside household tutor and sent him at once to convalesce in the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 挺之素歸心釋典，事僧惠義。

translations.literal: Tingzhi had long turned his heart to Buddhist scriptures and attended upon the monk Huiyi.
translations.idiomatic: Tingzhi had long devoted himself to Buddhist teaching and was a follower of the monk Huiyi.

sentences.zh: 及至東都，郁郁不得志，成疾。

translations.literal: When he reached the Eastern Capital he was depressed and unfulfilled in his ambitions and fell ill.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached the Eastern Capital he was despondent over his thwarted ambitions and fell ill.

sentences.zh: 自為墓誌曰：「天寶元年，嚴挺之自絳郡太守抗疏陳乞，天恩允請，許養疾歸閑，兼授太子詹事。

translations.literal: He himself composed an epitaph saying: "In the first year of Tianbao Yan Tingzhi, from his post as prefect of Jiang Commandery, submitted a forthright memorial stating his request; Heaven's grace granted it, permitting him to convalesce and return to leisure, and concurrently appointing him Household Tutor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote his own epitaph, which began: "In the first year of Tianbao, Yan Tingzhi, then prefect of Jiang Commandery, submitted a forthright memorial asking leave. Heaven's grace granted his request, allowing him to retire for his health and appointing him concurrently Household Tutor to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 前後歷任二十五官，每承聖恩，嘗忝獎擢，不盡驅策，駑蹇何階，仰答鴻造？

translations.literal: Before and after he held twenty-five official posts; each time he received the sage's grace and was once honored with promotion and advancement, yet could not fully exert himself—what steps has this lame nag to ascend and repay the vast creation?
translations.idiomatic: He had held twenty-five offices in all. Each time he received the emperor's favor and was honored with promotion, yet he could not fully repay that debt—what steps had this broken nag to climb in answering such vast grace?

sentences.zh: 春秋七十，無所展用，為人士所悲。

translations.literal: At seventy years of age he had nowhere to display his use; scholars and officials grieved for him.
translations.idiomatic: At seventy he had no scope left to serve, and men of standing mourned for him.

sentences.zh: 其年九月，寢疾，終於洛陽某裏之私第。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of that year he took to his bed with illness and died at his private residence in a certain lane of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of that year he took to his sickbed and died at his private residence in a lane of Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 十一月，葬於大照和尚塔次西原，禮也。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month he was buried on the western plain beside the pagoda of the monk Dazhao, as ritual required.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he was buried, as proper ritual dictated, on the western plain beside the pagoda of the monk Dazhao.

sentences.zh: 盡忠事君，叨載國史，勉拙從仕，或布人謠。

translations.literal: Serving the ruler with full loyalty, undeservedly recorded in the state histories; striving in clumsiness to follow office, sometimes spreading among the people's songs.
translations.idiomatic: He had served his sovereign with loyalty and been recorded, however undeservedly, in the state histories; he had done his clumsy best in office, and his name sometimes passed among the people's songs.

sentences.zh: 陵谷可以自紀，文章焉用為飾。

translations.literal: Hills and valleys can record oneself—of what use is literary ornament?
translations.idiomatic: The changing hills and valleys could serve as his own record; what need had he for literary ornament?

sentences.zh: 遺文薄葬，斂以時服。」

translations.literal: He left instructions for a plain burial and enshrouding in the garments of the season.
translations.idiomatic: He left instructions for a simple burial, to be laid in his ordinary clothes."

sentences.zh: 挺之與裴寬皆奉佛。

translations.literal: Tingzhi and Pei Kuan both practiced Buddhism.
translations.idiomatic: Tingzhi and Pei Kuan were both devoted Buddhists.

sentences.zh: 開元末，惠義卒，挺之服缞麻送於龕所。

translations.literal: At the end of Kaiyuan, Huiyi died; Tingzhi wore hemp mourning and escorted him to the niche shrine.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Kaiyuan reign Huiyi died; Tingzhi wore hemp mourning and escorted his remains to the shrine niche.

sentences.zh: 寬為河南尹，僧普寂卒，寬與妻子皆服缞绖，設次哭臨，妻子送喪至嵩山。

translations.literal: Kuan was Metropolitan Governor of Henan; when the monk Puji died, Kuan and his wife and children all wore hemp mourning, set up a mourning shelter and wept in attendance, and the wife and children escorted the funeral to Mount Song.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Kuan was Metropolitan Governor of Henan; when the monk Puji died, Kuan and his entire family wore mourning dress, set up a mourning shelter, and his wife and children escorted the funeral to Mount Song.

sentences.zh: 故挺之誌文云「葬於大照塔側」，祈其靈祐也。

translations.literal: Therefore Tingzhi's epitaph states "buried beside the Dazhao Pagoda," praying for its spiritual blessing.
translations.idiomatic: Hence Tingzhi's epitaph reads "buried beside the Dazhao Pagoda," seeking spiritual blessing there.

sentences.zh: 挺之素重交結，有許與，凡舊交先歿者，厚撫其妻子，凡嫁孤女數十人，時人重之。

translations.literal: Tingzhi had long valued forming bonds of friendship and kept his promises; for all old friends who died first he generously supported their wives and children, and in all he married off several tens of orphaned daughters; people of the time respected this.
translations.idiomatic: Tingzhi had long valued friendship and kept his promises; he generously supported the families of deceased friends and married off dozens of orphaned daughters; contemporaries greatly respected him for it.

sentences.zh: 子武，廣德中黃門侍郎、成都尹、劍南節度使。

translations.literal: His son Wu, in the Guangde era, served as Vice Director of the Yellow Gate, Governor of Chengdu, and Military Commissioner of Jiannan.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wu served in the Guangde era as Vice Director of the Yellow Gate, Governor of Chengdu, and Military Commissioner of Jiannan.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：崔日用附會三思，以取高位，預討韋氏，遂握重權。

translations.literal: The historian says: Cui Riyong attached himself to Sansi to gain high position, took part in suppressing the Wei clan, and thus grasped heavy power.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Cui Riyong attached himself to Wu Sansi to gain high office, took part in suppressing the Wei clan, and thus seized great power.

sentences.zh: 自言「吾一生行事，皆臨時制變，不必專守始謀」，信矣。

translations.literal: He said himself, "In all my life's actions I adapt on the spot and need not cling solely to the original plan"—how true that is.
translations.idiomatic: His own words—"Everything I have done in life I decided on the spot; there is no need to cling stubbornly to one's first plan"—are all too true.

sentences.zh: 與夫守死善道者，不可同年而語也。

translations.literal: He cannot be spoken of in the same year as those who hold to death in the good Way.
translations.idiomatic: He cannot be mentioned in the same breath as those who hold steadfast to the righteous path even unto death.

sentences.zh: 張嘉貞雖不立田園，奈急於勢利，朋比近習，杖姜皎、伷先，非中立之士也。

translations.literal: Although Zhang Jiazhen did not establish estates, alas he was eager for power and profit, formed factions with those near him, and had Jiang Jiao and Xianxian beaten with the staff—he was not a man of impartial standing.
translations.idiomatic: Though Zhang Jiazhen established no landed estates, he was eager for power and profit, formed factions with court intimates, and had Jiang Jiao and Pei Xianxian beaten—he was no impartial statesman.

sentences.zh: 蕭嵩位極中令，異政無聞，樹破虜之勛，真致遠之器。

translations.literal: Xiao Song reached the utmost as Director of the Secretariat; no distinctive policies are heard of, yet he built merit in defeating the barbarians—truly an instrument for reaching far.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Song rose to Director of the Secretariat without distinctive policies to his name, yet he built merit defeating foreign enemies—truly a man destined for far-reaching achievement.

sentences.zh: 九齡文學政事，咸有所稱，一時之選也。

translations.literal: Jiuling in literary arts and governmental affairs both had praise; he was the choice of his age.
translations.idiomatic: Jiuling won praise in both letters and government; he was the outstanding choice of his generation.

sentences.zh: 適之臨下雖簡，在公克勤，惜乎不得其死也！

translations.literal: Shizhi in dealing with subordinates was simple, yet in public affairs was able and diligent—alas that he did not meet a proper death!
translations.idiomatic: Shizhi was informal with subordinates but diligent in public affairs—alas that he did not die a proper death!

sentences.zh: 挺之才略器識，不下諸公，恥近權門，為人所惡，不登臺輔，養疾宮僚。

translations.literal: Tingzhi's talent, strategy, and discernment were not below the chief ministers; he was ashamed to draw near the gates of power, was hated by others, did not ascend to the terrace as chief minister, and nursed illness as a palace official.
translations.idiomatic: Tingzhi's talent and discernment matched the best of his peers; he scorned to court the powerful, earned enemies, never reached the chancellorship, and ended his days nursing illness as a palace official.

sentences.zh: 雖富貴在天，窮達有命，彼林甫者，誠可投畀豺虎也。

translations.literal: Although wealth and honor are in Heaven and failure and success have fate, that Linfu—he truly may be cast to wolves and tigers.
translations.idiomatic: Though wealth and honor come from Heaven and fortune has its own decree, that man Linfu truly deserves to be cast to wolves and tigers.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：開元之代，多士盈庭。

translations.literal: The encomium says: In the Kaiyuan age, many scholars filled the court.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium reads: In the Kaiyuan age, talented men filled the court.

sentences.zh: 日用無守，嘉貞近名。

translations.literal: Riyong had no constancy; Jiazhen courted reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Riyong lacked constancy; Jiazhen courted reputation.

sentences.zh: 嵩、齡、適、挺，各有度程。

translations.literal: Song, Ling, Shizhi, and Ting each had his measure and standard.
translations.idiomatic: Song, Jiuling, Shizhi, and Ting each had his own measure of worth.

sentences.zh: 大位俱極，半慚德馨。

translations.literal: They all reached the utmost in great position, yet were half ashamed before fragrant virtue.
translations.idiomatic: They all reached the highest offices, yet each fell somewhat short of true moral fragrance.
